This unblocks full #10372 MWE parity.
### Specializer metadata-erasure prevention + full value-parameter kind binding (Issues #10457/#10599)

Prevention work for the PR #10456 erasure class (#10423/#9420/#8869), plus the
bug it immediately caught. (1) New fixture
`dispatch/callspecialize_resolved_function_10457.jl` forces first-class
function arguments through both runtime-specialization entry points
(`CallSpecialize` sites and the `where`-parametric
`try_specialized_entry_for_runtime_call` bridge) while the callee body
materializes `PushResolvedFunction`; red-checked by reverting both #10456
hunks (16/18 assertions fail with `UndefVarError: identity`). (2) The
value-parameter load matrix added to `types_agg_value_params_10238.jl`
(Int64/Float64/Bool/Char/Symbol/Tuple through `(::VP{v}) where {v} = v`)
caught Issue #10599 on first run: the generic struct-tag arm of
`bind_type_params` only materialized i64-parsable and `:`-prefixed binding
names, so Float64/Bool/Char/Tuple value params leaked `DataType` wrappers into
method bodies. Fixed by parsing every value literal kind via the promoted
`parse_value_type_param_literal` (formerly `parse_val_tuple_element`) +
`bind_val_parameter_value`, and extending the `LoadTypeBinding` raw-value set
to narrow numerics. Residual (still open in #10599): `VP{Int8(5)}` normalizes
to `VP{Any}` at type instantiation. (3) CHECKLISTS.md gains the optimized
ForEach/counted-loop + specializer note: public iterator `length` is not
always an I64 loop bound; BigInt-backed ranges stay on generic `iterate`.
`String(v)` on a where-bound value parameter was found not to compile
(Issue #10597, unsupported-feature).

outer `T`, reversed braced order (`{S<:T, T}`), module-body definitions
(module bodies do not flow through the probed paths), and non-type bound
values (`T<:xval` with `xval = 5`; upstream raises `TypeError` — same
epic-tracked class, #10460/#10049). Definitions inside constant-false
branches are correctly NOT probed (pinned in the fixture after the
adversarial-verification review of PR #10594).
### Milestone 73 runtime definitions and Test values (Issues #10307, #10329, #10372, #10401)

Plain parametric aliases now retain both their compile-time annotation alias and
their runtime type-object binding, completing the #10372 MWE and #10501. Test
macros return upstream-shaped `Test.Result`/`DefaultTestSet` values (#10496).
Runtime eval/include installs mutable structs and evaluates field access
(#10329/#10563). Top-level control-flow struct definitions are reified through
the same runtime eval path, so only reached definitions become visible while
later constructor calls use opaque-eval dynamic dispatch (#10401).

### Retire the REPL `struct_instances` literal mirror (Issue #9784)

Fresh full-recompile fallback now reconstructs each persisted struct global once
from its authoritative `REPLGlobals` `StructRef` and `last_struct_heap`. The
parallel `struct_instances: HashMap<String, Literal>` field, extraction writes,
reset handling, stale-literal removal, and second assignment replay are deleted.
Forced-full-recompile regressions cover one-instance heap identity and preserve
mutable structs, Complex/Rational values, nested empty arrays, arrays of structs,
and value-carried structs with non-reconstructible `Base.Pairs` fields. This is a
partial #9784 retirement; the other fresh fallback mirrors remain live.

### Empty filtered generator eltype for function-call predicates (Issue #10138)

All-filtered generators whose predicate depends on a user function call now match
upstream's empty semantics: `collect(f(x) for x in xs if f(x) >= k)` produces
`Vector{Union{}}`, and `sum(...)` raises `ArgumentError` instead of returning
`0`. Transparent predicates such as `x >= k` and known Base predicates such as
`isodd(x)` still keep the inferred empty eltype, preserving the Issue #9127
fast path. Runtime FilterMap finalization now checks predicate inlining markers
before trusting a compile-time empty eltype.

Regression coverage: `generator/filtered_generator_empty_user_predicate_10138.jl`
checks function-call predicate collect/sum semantics, operator-body predicates,
and transparent predicate controls. The separate non-identity mapped-body empty
`sum` gap is tracked as Issue #10618.

### Vector{SubArray} structural equality with Vector{Vector} (Issue #10296)

Array `==` fallback now treats nested array-like elements through the same
logical ArrayValue view used for top-level array equality. A `SubArray` element
inside a collected iterator result therefore compares element-wise against a
plain `Vector` literal instead of falling back to wrapper identity or debug
representation.

Regression coverage: `subarray/vector_subarray_vector_equality_10296.jl` checks
`SubArray == Vector`, both operand orders, nested `Vector{SubArray}` vs
`Vector{Vector}`, and `collect(Iterators.partition(...))` against the equivalent
nested vector literal.

### where-binder shadowing `Module` rebinds the `CoreType::Module` leaf (Issue #10299)

`CoreType::rebind_where_binders` gained the missing `CoreType::Module(n) if
is_binder(n)` arm (the second concrete instance of the missing-arm class after
`Any`, from the PR #10231 codex review): a `where` binder spelled `Module`
shadows the builtin `Core.Module` type, but the kept `UnionAll`'s body retained
the raw unrebound `CoreType::Module("Module")` leaf, so
`(Vector{Module} where Module<:Real) == (Vector{T} where T<:Real)` returned
`false` (upstream: `true`; `<:` masked the gap via the mutual-subtype
fallback). The remaining leaf variants recognized by
`julia_type_references_typevar`'s generic name check were audited: `Bottom`
renders as `Union{}` and `Value` holds literals, neither spellable as a binder
identifier. Regression testset added to
`tests/fixtures/types/where_binder_shadow_scope_10100.jl` (verified against
upstream Julia 1.12).

### Single-variable comprehensions over iterate-only structs (Issue #10442)

Single-variable array comprehensions now drive the `iterate` protocol for
struct-typed iterators instead of assuming every non-generator iterable supports
public `getindex`. This fixes `Iterators.partition` and other length-bearing
custom iterators that intentionally provide `iterate` but no indexing, while
leaving the existing eager index loop for arrays and ranges intact.

Regression coverage: `comprehension/partition_iterate_protocol_10442.jl`
checks variable-bound and inline `partition(...)` comprehensions, filtered
partition comprehensions, a custom `length` + `iterate` struct with no
`getindex`, and confirms public `q[1]` remains unavailable.
### Prevention: owner-scoped UnionAll TypeVar projection identity (Issue #10420)

Prevention follow-up for #10412. Added the dedicated regression fixture
`reflection/typevar_projection_owner_identity_10420.jl` — order is
load-bearing: it FIRST populates the constructed-TypeVar cache with a user
`TypeVar(:T)` / `TypeVar(:K)` / `TypeVar(:V)` via `Vector{T}` / `Dict{K,V}`
(`Vector{T}.parameters[1] === T`), THEN asserts the owner-scoped wrapper-chain
identities (`Vector.var === Vector.body.parameters[1]`, Dict two-binder
chain) and that the two identity domains stay separate (`!== T`). Verified
14/14 green under upstream julia 1.12 and sjulia main, and 7/14 red at the
pre-fix commit `e4336b2c2`. Added the VM unit test
`reflection_parameter_to_value_for_owner_prefers_owner_scoped_projection_issue_10420`
(owner-local projection cache beats the global constructed-TypeVar cache while
the ownerless constructed path keeps the user identity; negative-tested by
flipping the precedence). Documented the identity-domain rule in
`docs/vm/CHECKLISTS.md` ("Runtime TypeVar projection identity domains").
Residual read-order sensitivity (body `.parameters` before `.var`, and `.var`
before constructing `Dict{K,V}`) diverges from upstream in both directions and
is filed as Issue #10603.

### Preserve nested empty-array element types across REPL full recompiles (Issue #10581)

`empty_array_init_expr` now resolves heap-backed array wrappers through the
committed struct heap before deriving their Julia element type. A nested `Int[]`
inside a persisted struct therefore reconstructs as `Int[]`, not `Any[]`; after a
forced fresh full recompile, `push!(..., 7)` reads back `7::Int64` like upstream.
The non-wrapper carrier fallback uses the resolved `ArrayValue` element tag.

### Nested array element types through Memory and runtime literals (Issue #10495)

Array construction paths whose element type is itself a concrete array type now
preserve the nested element type instead of widening to `Any`. Runtime
`DataType` to `ArrayElementType` conversion maps `Vector{T}` / `Matrix{T}` /
`Array{T,N}` to boxed logical tags, `Memory{T}` constructor lowering reuses the
same concrete-parametric fallback as typed empty literals, and runtime-valued
array literals join array-like Julia types by rank and promoted inner element
type. The `collect(::Tuple)` JuliaType tfunc now returns
`Vector{promote_typeof(tuple fields)}`, which lets `[collect(...), ...]`
allocate `Memory{Vector{T}}` rather than `Memory{Any}`.

Regression coverage: `array/nested_array_eltype_10495.jl` checks copy
constructors, `Vector{Vector{T}}(undef, n)`, `similar`, `Memory{Vector{T}}`,
`map(collect, ...)`, runtime-valued nested array literals, promoted inner
numeric eltypes, and matrix-valued element tags.
### Union type value を独立 kind として分類し branch field a/b を公開 (Issue #10313)

`Union{Int64,Float64}` のような Union type value が `isa`/dispatch 分類経路で
素の `DataType` と誤分類されていた (`u isa DataType` → true / `u isa Union` →
false / `u.a` → FieldError)。`typeof` は Issue #5335 の special case で正しく
`Union` を返していたが、`isa` が使う `RuntimeTypeRegistry::kind_for` に Union
kind が無かったのが根本原因。`RuntimeTypeObjectKind::Union` を追加して
registry を typeof/isa 共通の単一情報源にし (`typeof` 側の special case は
削除)、`runtime_type_projection` が `Union` を返すことで
`isa DataType`=false / `isa Union`=true / `isa UnionAll`=false /
`isa Type`=true が upstream julia 1.12 と一致。branch field は
`RuntimeTypeObject::union_branch_field` が upstream `jl_type_union` の正規形
(`canonicalize_union`, Issue #5066 の既存実装: singleton < isbits < other
DataType < UnionAll、同順位はアルファベット順、右結合ネスト) を投影し、
`u.a === Float64` / `u.b === Int64` /
`Union{Int,Float64,String}.b === Union{Int64,String}` を dot access と
`getfield` の両経路 (exec/struct_ops.rs と builtins_reflection) で返す。
未知フィールドは upstream 同様 `FieldError(Union, :c)` を報告する。
Fixture: `tests/fixtures/types/union_isa_branch_fields_10313.jl`。

### Where-binder trio from PR #10231 verified fixed and closed (Issues #10301, #10302, #10303)

The three bugs found during PR #10231's Issue #10100 work — `JuliaType::from_name`
container arms mismatching a trailing where-clause (#10301), infinite recursion in
nested same-name where-binder bound resolution (#10302), and parenthesized nested
where-expressions bypassing structural where-lowering (#10303) — were verified fixed
on main. The fixes landed structurally via PR #10411 (`lower_where_body_expr`
ParenthesizedExpression unwrap + `typevar_bound_value_expr` same-name outer-binder
bound substitution, Issue #10274) and PR #10454 (scoped CoreTypeVar matcher
identity, Issue #10279), which supersede the intermediate branch-state fixes the
issue bodies describe. Both MWE spellings (`Vector{T} where T<:T where T<:Real`
and the parenthesized form) now produce `isa == true` matching upstream julia
1.12.6, with no stack-overflow abort. Regression coverage for the unparenthesized
chain spelling added to
`tests/fixtures/types/where_bound_undefvarerror_10226.jl` (the parenthesized form
was already covered there by PR #10411). Residual: sjulia collapses the redundant
inner binder in `show` (`Vector{T} where T<:Real` vs upstream's
`Vector{T} where {T<:Real, T<:T}`) — display-parity follow-up filed as Issue #10572.
### supertype on the BitArray family threads the fixed Bool parameter (Issue #10312)

`supertype(BitVector)` / `supertype(BitMatrix)` / `supertype(BitArray)` now
return `AbstractVector{Bool}` / `AbstractMatrix{Bool}` / `AbstractArray{Bool}`
(and `supertype(BitArray{N})` returns `AbstractArray{Bool, N}` for N≥3),
matching upstream Julia 1.12. The BitArray family are zero-free-typevar
concrete aliases (`BitVector = BitArray{1}` with
`BitArray{N} <: AbstractArray{Bool,N}`), so their supertype always carries the
fixed `Bool` element parameter — which the context-free
`builtin_struct_direct_supertype_name` table's bare `&'static str` names
cannot thread. The reflection layer (`dense_array_alias_supertype_name` in
`vm/type_objects.rs`) now resolves the family before that table, following the
same element-threading pattern as the `Vector{T}` fix (#10282/#10283). The
subtype-hierarchy table itself is unchanged.

### Dynamic-base Core.apply_type splats (Issue #10191)

`Core.apply_type(base, args...)` now accepts a runtime `UnionAll` base held in
a local or passed through a function parameter. The compiler carries the raw
call-argument splat mask in `ApplyTypeDynamicSplat`; the VM expands each marked
collection before selecting the first flattened value as the base (Issue
#10555), then applies the remaining flat list through the same runtime
`UnionAll` instantiation used by positional dynamic application. That path now
enforces binder bounds, arity, and concrete-base rejection (Issue #10554).
Static-base calls use that same validated runtime path, and partial application
substitutes earlier parameters into dependent upper and lower bounds (Issue
#10570). Parametric abstract-type metadata retains complete `TypeParam` bounds,
so abstract wrappers use the same runtime bound and arity checks. The former
zero-argument concrete-type wrapper recovery is replaced by
`a.name.wrapper`; canonical wrapper identity remains tracked by Issue #10558.
`typejoin` no longer needs its 16-argument W-64 dispatch and now calls the
upstream-shaped `Core.apply_type(wrapper, subst...)` directly. The regression
covers base and parameter splats, multiple splat segments, partial and builtin
wrappers, TypeVar/value parameters, empty splats, negative parity cases, and a
17-parameter wrapper.

### Typed-loop recognizer scope tracker #10477 resolved by audit + split (Issue #10477)

Scope item 4 (compound `while c1 && c2` conditions) audited: the general
recognizer already accepts the compound guard (I64 counter AND F64 threshold)
and executes it natively — pinned by
`typed_loop_recognizes_compound_while_condition_10477`. The remaining scope
items were split into dedicated issues with the current blocker analysis:
array-store/map-copy loops → #10566 (root blocker newly diagnosed: runtime
specialization never fires for MemoryRef-backed struct-Vector arguments, so
the #6346 `IndexStoreTyped; StoreSlotArray` shape is unreachable in practice;
plus the #7538 decoder reject and the write-through bridge, with a
transactional-buffer design), String-op loops → #10559, Dict-op loops →
#10560, nested-loop nativization → #10561.

### Block-entry inlining of small I64 callees into typed loops (Issue #10516)

`execute_typed_loop_block` now splices small resolved I64 callee bodies
(≤ 32 ops, no nested callees, translatable ops, exact arg-count stack depth)
directly into the typed-loop op stream at block entry, covering both
`CallI64Function` and `CallSpecializeI64Function` sites while inheriting the
specialize path's per-entry cache-invalidation contract. A new
`UninitI64Slot` op reproduces the frame-less executor's per-call `local_init`
reset, keeping load-before-store bail semantics identical. coprime-π
`calc_pi_n5000` (cold CLI): ~3.62 s → ~2.82 s (~22%); the 25M in-loop
`execute_i64_function_block` calls drop to the 5k interpreted-outer-loop
residue.

### NamedTuple-returning broadcast materializes typed arrays (Issue #10469)

Broadcasting a function that returns a `NamedTuple` now matches upstream for
the representative vector and matrix materialization surfaces. `combine_eltypes`
samples the broadcast result and returns `typeof(result)` for `NamedTuple`
values, `_broadcasted_similar` allocates through `_array_undef_from_dims` for
`@NamedTuple{...}` / `NamedTuple{...}` element types, and the runtime array
store path treats `Value::NamedTuple` as a boxed element rather than falling
through to numeric coercion. Runtime type-object allocation also preserves
`NamedTuple` element tags as abstract boxed storage, so the result reports
`Vector{@NamedTuple{...}}` / `Matrix{@NamedTuple{...}}` instead of
`Vector{Any}`.

Regression coverage: `broadcast/namedtuple_return_10469.jl` checks same-typed
and mixed-field `NamedTuple` vectors plus 2-D matrix broadcast, including value,
`typeof`, `eltype`, and shape parity.

### Milestone 73 syntax/lowering compatibility batch (Issues #10444, #10475, #10506, #10511, #10518, #10519)

Array separator state now rejects the symmetric illegal `;;`/space mix and
preserves `;;`-newline row continuation through CST lowering. Typed empty ncat
literals retain rank and element type, dotted calls accept parametric/value
callees, immutable field assignment raises at runtime, and literal tuple
destructuring retains its complete tail value through explicit IR identity.

### Typed-loop inlining of untyped Float64 callees (Issue #10491)

The F64 mirror of #10439: a `LoadSlotF64` run feeding `CallSpecialize` now
fuses to `CallSpecializeF64Slots` (+`@inbounds` twin), backed by an all-`F64`
specialize dispatch cache (`specialization_f64_cache` / fast cache,
`record_f64_spec_dispatch`) and inlined into typed loops as
`TypedLoopOp::CallSpecializeF64Function` with the same
runtime-resolve-or-bail contract as the I64 op. Two F64-specific pieces:
`install_specialized_body` now slotizes runtime-specialized bodies against the
SPECIALIZED argument/store types (`slot::build_specialized_slot_types`) instead
of the fallback's `unknown` tags, and the resolved callee may be the
mixed-type frame-less `TypedScalarFunctionBlock` (`ResolvedSpecF64Callee`),
since all-F64 helpers usually carry an I64 loop counter. The #10491 MWE
(`scan(2000)`, untyped `fstep`) runs ~0.38 s vs ~1.84 s for the fully-typed
twin (whose `CallResolved` site cannot inline mixed-type callees yet — Issue
#10542). Parity fixture covers NaN/±Inf/signed-zero/rounding.

### Pair iterator-like operations (Issue #10476)

`Pair` now behaves as a 2-element iterable for the common upstream surfaces that
were missing: `last(Pair(1, 2))`, `collect(Pair(1, 2))`, `sum(Pair(1, 2))`, and
positional splat `f(Pair(1, 2)...)` all match upstream. `pair.jl` defines the
2-step `iterate` protocol, `length`, runtime `eltype`, iterator traits, and a
typed `collect(::Pair)` so same-typed pairs produce `Vector{Int64}` rather than
falling through to `Any`. The VM splat helper now expands runtime `Pair` structs
to their `first`/`second` fields, including heap-backed values carried across
REPL eval boundaries.

Regression coverage: `pair_iterator_operations_10476.jl`, a VM splat unit test,
and the #9793 value-carried-container REPL differential corpus now includes Pair
`last`/`collect`/`sum`/splat.

### AoT: sibling `let`-block same-name locals get independent, precisely-typed storage (Issue #10251 / #10111)

The AoT IR converter keyed each local variable's storage slot and static Rust
type on the bare **variable name**, so two sibling top-level `let` blocks that
each bound a same-named local to a *different* concrete numeric type were unified
onto one slot: the later binding either truncated (`i8::try_from(144)` →
spurious `InexactError`) or, when whole-program inference widened the name to
`Any`, emitted non-compiling `let mut r: Value = Value::from(i8_value)` (the
runtime `Value` enum has no `Int8`/`UInt8` variant, so `Value: From<i8>` is
unimplemented; boxing would also report `typeof` as `Int64`).

`IrConverter` now treats each `let` block as a nested lexical scope: a scope
stack (`enter_lexical_scope`/`exit_lexical_scope`) makes a binding's scope its
identity, so a fresh binding in a sibling scope is independent of a same-named
binding elsewhere, and a fresh binding inside a `let` body is typed by its own
initializer instead of the cross-scope-widened union. Two sibling `let` blocks
flatten into one Rust scope and rely on Rust shadowing
(`let mut r: i8` … `let mut r: u8`), matching Julia's lexical scoping and the
already-correct VM interpreter. Leaked bindings (`x = let ... end`,
`@time xs = ...`) keep their enclosing-scope type via env restore. Design:
`docs/vm/AOT_VARIABLE_IDENTITY.md`. Tests:
`aot_e2e_tests::test_aot_sibling_let_same_name_distinct_types_10251` /
`..._int_float_10251`, fixture `tests/fixtures/aot/scope_sibling_rebind_10251.jl`.
The sibling `for`-loop variant (name-keyed `compute_hoisted_locals`) and
same-scope type-changing reassignment remain out of scope — tracked in #10523.

### Alias-preserving shared-Rc transplant compaction (Issue #9827)

- Removed the shared-Rc verbatim fallback from `reachable_compacted_struct_heap`.
- Clone array, memory, Ref, and WeakRef carriers through one identity map shared
  by retained heap fields and seed roots, preserving aliases and cycles while
  detaching the candidate from session state before remapping.
- Guard shared-array `===` identity, source-Rc non-mutation, and 1000-eval heap
  boundedness with regression tests.
### AoT: keep scope-local `Any` joins boxed as `Value` (Issue #10537)

`enter_lexical_scope` (Issue #10251) only preserved boxed slots for
`StaticType::Union`, but `unify_types(Any, T) == Any` — so a `let` local
reassigned through an Any-returning call (`x = 1; x = g("s")` with
`g(::Any)::Any`) dropped the env entry, declared `i64` from the first
assignment, and failed codegen storing `Any` into that slot (#6978). The
dynamic boundary now matches `stmt.rs` and keeps both `Any` and `Union`.
Tests: `type_unstable_any_return_reassignment_uses_value_slot_issue_10537`,
`aot_e2e_tests::test_aot_let_any_return_reassignment_uses_value_slot_10537`.
Caught by codex review on #10528.

### Generalized typed-loop bail/side-effect transactionality guard (Issue #10504)

A typed-loop bail re-runs the whole block generically from the loop header, so
any data-dependent bail (`ModI64`/`LoadModI64Slot` on `x % 0` / `typemin % -1`,
`IndexLoad*`, `CallI64Function`/`CallF64Function`/`CallSpecializeI64Function`
whose callee bails) that fires AFTER an in-place side effect (`RandF64`,
`IndexStore*`) double-applied the effect — `typemin % -1` bails silently
(upstream yields 0), making the re-drawn RNG stream observable wrong output.
The recognizer now rejects any block mixing the two op classes
(`typed_loop_op_can_bail_on_data` × `typed_loop_op_is_in_place_side_effect`),
subsuming the earlier #10104 (IndexLoad-only) and #10439 (specialize-call-only)
guards. Hot kernels (coprime-π gcd, Monte-Carlo rand, IFS LCG) contain at most
one class and keep the native path.

### Retire `ComplexF64MandelbrotEscapeLoopBlock` via typed-loop Complex recurrence fusion (Issue #10532)

The hand-written `ComplexF64MandelbrotEscapeLoopBlock` executable block is removed.
In its place, the generic typed-loop path now recognizes and fuses the SROA'd
`Complex{Float64}` recurrence `z = z*z + c` into a single
`TypedLoopOp::ComplexMulAddAssign` superinstruction. A predecode-time
`fuse_complex_mul_add_assign` pass collapses the 8-op SROA expansion
(`PushDiffSquaresF64Slots`, two `PushMulF64Slots`, `AddF64`, slot stores,
`CopyF64Slots`) into one op that updates the unboxed `(z_re, z_im)` slot pair
in place. The executor computes the same result as the pure-Julia
`Base.:*(::ComplexF64, ::ComplexF64)` followed by `Base.:+`, so concrete
`mandel_point(c::ComplexF64, ...)` loops no longer need a bespoke Rust kernel.

Tests that asserted the old block now assert the typed-loop path and the
absence of the block profiler counter. The abstract `::Complex` route still uses
a residual Rust fast path for `*` and `abs2` (Issue #10530, W-66) until the
pure-Julia dispatch path is fast enough on its own.

### Runtime specializer gives ComplexF64 SROA bodies enough local slots (Issue #10567)

Runtime-specialized functions that decompose `Complex{Float64}` into unboxed
`(re, im)` slot pairs (`__sjulia_cx_re_*` / `__sjulia_cx_im_*` synthetic locals)
now allocate a frame sized for the specialized body instead of reusing the
fallback function's smaller `local_slot_count`. The specializer emits
`JumpIfGtI64` for `for` loops with `Int64` upper bounds, and
`install_specialized_body` remaps synthetic locals to fresh slot indices and
reports the required slot count. `SpecializedCode` carries that count, and the
I64/F64 specialize dispatch caches and `CallSpecialize` execution path size their
frames from the chosen entry.

This lets untyped `mandel_point(c, maxiter)` (no `::ComplexF64` annotations)
take the same SROA'd, typed-loop path as the typed version once the runtime
specializer sees concrete `ComplexF64` arguments. The scalar for-loop benchmark
at 1500×1500/maxiter=500 drops from ~610 s to ~38 s on the generic VM path;
`sjulia VM typed` stays at ~2.3 s. Regression tests
`complex_mandelbrot_escape_runtime_specialization_uses_typed_loop_6253` and
`complex_mandelbrot_escape_k_minus_one_uses_typed_loop_8796` verify the
typed-loop path is used.

### `collect(Iterators.flatten(...))` over generators recovers the concrete eltype (Issue #9438)

`collect` of an `Iterators.flatten` whose inner iterables are `Base.Generator`s
now recovers the concrete element type via value-based `grow_to!` widening
(`Vector{Int64}`, promoted `Vector{Float64}`) instead of widening to
`Vector{Any}`. Root cause: sjulia hardcoded `IteratorEltype(::Flatten) =
HasEltype()`, so `collect` always joined `eltype(::Generator)==Any` into
`Vector{Any}`. Upstream's `IteratorEltype(::Type{Flatten{I}}) =
_flatteneltype(I, IteratorEltype(I))` marks a flatten's eltype known only when
BOTH the outer iterator AND its element type (the inner iterables) have a known
eltype; a `Generator` is `EltypeUnknown()`, routing `collect` to
`grow_to!`. `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/iterators.jl` now mirrors this at the
value level, with a per-field `Union{Tuple,NamedTuple}` method reproducing the
upstream tuple/NamedTuple special case (so empty typed inners like
`(Int8[], Int16[]) -> Vector{Signed}` and tuple-of-generators ->
`Vector{Int64}` both match upstream). Fixture:
`tests/fixtures/iterators/iterators_flatten_generator_eltype_9438.jl` (18 assertions,
julia-parity checked). One increment of the iterator-trait-algebra debt tracked in
#10050 / #10463 (the broader `IteratorSize`/`HasShape` wrapper propagation and the
static-eltype-for-empty-concrete-container gap remain).
### Legacy REPL selector と oracle を退役した (Issue #9784 partial)

Rust 内部の `EvalModel` selector、Legacy compile/carry 分岐、Legacy test/benchmark
比較を削除した。REPL corpus の安全網は upstream 確認済み golden と persistent
決定性検証として維持した。Persistent の full-recompile fallback が使う retirement-list
bookkeeping は残しており、Issue #9784 自体は完了扱いにしない。

### Constant-bounded compare-and-branch peephole fusion (Issue #10105)

The peephole optimizer now folds slot-vs-constant I64 guards into
`JumpIfCmpI64SlotConst` for all six predicates, covering both directional
jumps and compare-plus-false-branch forms. Jump-target relocation and
typed-loop reconstruction preserve existing control-flow behavior. Other
suggested patterns were either already implemented or absent from emitted
bytecode.

### Typed loops for read-only 1-D numeric array reductions (Issue #10104)

The typed-loop recognizer now accepts F64/I64 one-dimensional array loads and
executes read-only reductions natively. Memory-backed Julia arrays are resolved
through a read-only snapshot at block entry; blocks containing array stores or
other replay-unsafe effects remain on the interpreter path. Runtime type or
bounds mismatches bail out before committing scalar slots, preserving catchable
errors. Array-store, String/Dict, and nested-loop coverage remains in #10477.

### Stack VM: argument-vector pool for the direct-call paths (Issue #10103)

The general direct-call paths allocated a fresh argument vector on every call,
including tight recursive workloads. Since arguments are cloned into callee
slots, the vector is scratch storage: the VM now reuses it through a bounded
`arg_vec_pool`, and the direct-call helpers borrow `&[Value]` so ownership
stays at the fill site. Each in-flight recursive call owns a vector removed
from the pool, and `MAX_POOLED_ARG_VECS = 256` bounds retained capacity.

### 配列リテラルの区切り文字 leniency バグ修正 (Issue #10398)

sjulia が `julia --startup-file=no` (1.12.6, JuliaSyntax.jl) が `ParseError`
とする配列リテラルの区切り文字の組み合わせを寛容に受理していた: (a) スペース
区切りの行 (`[1 2 ...]`) の後に続く `;;`(ちょうど2連続)が、直後の改行による
「行の折り返し」でない場合(`[1 2;; 3 4]`); (b) `;`-run がスペースで分断され
る場合 (`[1 2; ; 3 4]`); (c) `;`-run が改行で分断される場合
(`[1 2;\n;3 4]`)。`Parser::consume_row_separator_run`
(`subset_julia_vm_parser/src/parser/collections.rs`) が `Newline`/`Semicolon`
トークンを区別なく1つの run として吸収していたのが原因。新設
`array_literal_is_row_major` で既に構築済みの `MatrixRow`/`Semicolon` CST
から row-major 状態を判定し、run が改行で終わらない `;;`(2連続)の混在と、
run 内部のスペース分断を reject するよう修正。未typed/typed 両方の4呼び出し
箇所が同じ関数を共有するため一箇所の修正で揃って直る。既存の `;;;`(3連続以
上)は upstream 同様チェック対象外のため #10190/#10378 の N 次元 shape
folding fixture は無変更で green。関連: 対称方向(列優先確立後のスペース行)
は #10518、既存(regression でない)の複数行 `;;\n` line-wrap lowering gap は
#10519 で追跡。

### Metamorphic equivalence-lane harness (Issue #10465; parent #10452)

`scripts/metamorphic_equivalence.sh` — a manifest-driven differential harness
asserting `normalize(run(prog, lane A)) == normalize(run(transform(prog), lane B))`
over the SAME sjulia binary (sjulia-vs-sjulia, not upstream parity). All five
#10465 lanes are implemented:

- **direct_callable** — `f(x)` vs `Base.f(x)` vs `g=f; g(x)` vs `map(f,[x])[1]`,
  comparing result value + result type + exception class. Corpus:
  `tests/equivalence/direct_callable.tsv`. This is exactly the #10187/#10250
  divergence family.
- **module_wrap** — run a corpus file at Main top-level vs inside a generated
  unique `module`, comparing at the observation boundary (generated module
  prefix + source line/col normalized away). Corpus:
  `tests/equivalence/module_wrap/*.jl`.
- **fresh_cache** — run a corpus file with persistent caches disabled vs after
  priming an isolated persistent-cache target and observing the restored-cache
  lane from a second process. Corpus: `tests/equivalence/fresh_cache/*.jl`.
- **generic_optimized** — run a corpus file with `SJULIA_SSA_PIPELINE=0` vs the
  default optimized SSA pipeline. Corpus:
  `tests/equivalence/generic_optimized/*.jl`.
- **vm_aot** — run a documented AoT acceptance fixture through the VM vs a
  `juliars --minimal-prelude --emit-binary` generated binary. Corpus:
  `tests/equivalence/vm_aot.tsv`.

Divergences are Issue-linked and two-sided via
`docs/vm/EQUIVALENCE_KNOWN_DIVERGENCES.tsv` (a registered divergence that later
AGREES fails as STALE; a new un-registered divergence fails the gate). Wrap-unsafe
patterns are documented in `docs/vm/EQUIVALENCE_MODULE_WRAP_EXCLUSIONS.tsv`. The
harness carries its own `--selftest` negative control (value/type/exception
comparators each proven to fire on a seeded divergence, plus a positive control),
and is automatically selected by guarded premerge for semantic-pipeline paths;
`bash scripts/premerge_gate.sh --metamorphic` forces it elsewhere. The VM/AoT
manifest covers all three acceptance kernels. Running it surfaced a real bug
(#10512, `map(string,[42])[1]` type-error divergence); after the bug was fixed,
the stale-row ratchet removed the known-divergence row.

### Base cache schema fingerprint sync is now enforced in-suite (Issue #10051 slice, Root Cause #1)

A `CACHE_VERSION` bump requires a hand-run `base_cache_schema_fingerprint.txt`
`--update`; when forgotten, `scripts/audit_base_cache_schema_fingerprint.sh`
only goes red in CI (disabled here) or `premerge_gate.sh` at merge time, so the
drift lands on `main` (recurring: #9498, the #10440 `CACHE_VERSION` 95→96→97
churn, and a live 97→98 drift that was red on `main` when this landed). A new
`#[cfg(test)]` module `subset_julia_vm_compile/src/compile/schema_fingerprint_guard.rs`
recomputes the fingerprint with the audit's exact byte-order algorithm and fails
a plain `cargo nextest run --lib` (naming the exact `--update` command) whenever
the committed snapshot drifts from `CACHE_VERSION` or the schema sources — so the
drift surfaces in the normal local loop and the full suite, not only when someone
remembers to run the bash audit. It reads the same three inputs the audit reads
(manifest, schema sources, `CACHE_VERSION` parsed from `precompile.rs` text) and
is deliberately NOT listed in `base_cache_schema_files.txt`, so it never perturbs
the fingerprint it measures. Ships with the required negative self-test
(`stale_snapshot_is_detected`) plus a `recomputed_fingerprint_matches_build_rs_embedded_hash`
test that machine-checks the `LC_ALL=C`-vs-`Path`-sort "coincidence" the audit
header flagged as unproven. The bash audit remains the single snapshot writer and
`deserialize_base_cache` remains the runtime corruption guard — unchanged; this is
purely versioning/fingerprint SYNC ergonomics (broader #10051 determinism/coupling
scope stays open).

### Generalized the I64/F64 scalar function-block IR (Issue #10427)

PR #10309 (`I64FunctionBlock`) と PR #10426 (`F64FunctionBlock`) が重複させて
いた frame-less スカラー関数ブロック機構を、スカラー要素型 `S` (`i64`/`f64`) で
ジェネリックな 1 実装に統合した (`subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/executable.rs`)。導入した
抽象は `ScalarKind` トレイト (+ `I64Kind`/`F64Kind`)、`ScalarFunctionOp<S>` /
`ScalarFunctionBlock<S>` / `ScalarFunctionSlot` / `ScalarFunctionBuilder<'a,S>` /
`ScalarRelation`、および単一のミニインタプリタ `execute_scalar_function_block::<K>`。
型固有の詳細 (F64 の NaN/順序比較、I64 のラップ算術・Euclidean modulo、型別 base
unary `abs`、predecode の命令マッピング、compare-branch fusion、per-type キャッシュ)
はローカルに保持。`I64FunctionBlock`/`F64FunctionBlock`/`F64FunctionOp` 等は後方
互換エイリアスとして残し、`#[doc(hidden)]` の F64 テスト API を維持。単相化により
コード生成は従来と同等で、coprime-π (`calc_pi_benchmark`) と関数インライン Mandelbrot
(`f64_mandelbrot_function_inline_benchmark`) の VM ベンチに退行なし。設計ノート:
[SCALAR_FUNCTION_BLOCK.md](./SCALAR_FUNCTION_BLOCK.md)。

### `@nospecialize`/`@specialize` の値位置評価を upstream に一致 (Issue #10323)

`x = @nospecialize(42)` のような **値位置**での `@nospecialize`/`@specialize`
呼び出しが、これまで引数をそのまま返していた(`42`)のを、upstream の
`Base.@nospecialize`/`@specialize`(`base/essentials.jl`)が常に
`Expr(:meta, :nospecialize, vars...)` へ展開し、それを実行時に評価すると
包んだ式を**評価せずに** `nothing` になる挙動に一致させた。
`lowering/expr/macros/mod.rs` の式位置マクロディスパッチ
(`lower_macro_expr` / `lower_macro_expr_with_ctx`)に `"nospecialize" |
"specialize"` の専用アームを追加し、`Expr::Literal(Literal::Nothing, span)`
を返すのみで引数式を lower しない(副作用なしを upstream と一致させる)。
シグネチャ位置 (`f(@nospecialize(x)) = x`, `lowering/function/signature.rs`)
と文位置 (`@nospecialize x y`, `lowering/stmt/macros/mod.rs`) は元々別経路
で upstream と一致済みのため変更なし。fixture:
`tests/fixtures/macros/nospecialize.jl` に値位置 testset を追加(副作用が
発生しないことも assert)。

### Typed loops inline untyped I64 callees reached through `CallSpecializeI64Slots` (Issue #10439)

An untyped scalar helper (`mygcd(a, b)`) called from a typed loop through a
`CallSpecializeI64Slots` site used to keep the whole caller loop on the generic
interpreter (`SJULIA_TYPED_LOOP_DEBUG=1` →
`reason=unsupported-instr:CallSpecializeI64Slots`), even though the callee body
was already frame-less-specialized. The typed-loop recognizer
(`try_predecode_typed_ops_range`, loop mode only) now accepts
`CallSpecializeI64Slots`/`CallSpecializeInboundsI64Slots` and emits
`TypedLoopOp::CallSpecializeI64Function`, which resolves the callee's live I64
specialization (`specialization_i64_cache` → `resolve_specialize_i64_callee`) at
block-execution time and runs the *same* predecoded body the generic hit path
runs. Any resolution miss or an un-decodable body bails to the generic
interpreter (frame untouched), so the result is bit-for-bit identical and cache
invalidation is inherited. `benchmarks/calc_pi_n5000.jl` (untyped) drops from
~9.8 s to ~3.6 s — within ~16 % of the fully-typed twin (3.1 s); the N=2000 case
is 4.48 s → 0.52 s (≈8.6×). Correctness pinned by
`tests/fixtures/loops/typed_loop_call_specialize_i64_10439.jl` (untyped-in-loop
== typed twin == upstream Julia across negative modulo / zero / Int64 overflow).
Design note: `docs/vm/CALL_INSTRUCTIONS.md`. The Float64 mirror is deferred (no
`CallSpecializeF64Slots` instruction / F64 dispatch cache) — Issue #10491.

### Cache predecoded I64 function blocks in the CallSpecializeI64Slots fast path (Issue #10508)

PR #10498 made untyped Int64 callees inside typed loops fast by specializing
and inlining them via `CallSpecializeI64Slots`. This change removes the
remaining per-call HashMap probes on that hot path:

- `fast_primitive_binary_both` is checked first in `execute_binary_both` so
  primitive `Int64`/`Float64` pairs short-circuit before generic dispatch.
- The `CallSpecializeI64Slots` handler reads small-arity `I64` arguments from
  a fixed stack array instead of allocating a `Vec`.
- `specialization_i64_fast_cache` is a direct `Vec` lookup by `spec_func_index`
  (replacing the `(spec_func_index, arity)` HashMap lookup) and stores an
  `I64SpecFastCacheEntry { arity, dispatch, predecoded }`.
- The predecoded `I64FunctionBlock` is cached alongside the dispatch metadata,
  so the hot path executes the block by reference without touching
  `i64_function_cache` at all.

Result on `benchmarks/calc_pi_n*.jl` (cache-embedded CLI, warm run):
untyped N=5000 ~4.06 s, N=10000 ~17.37 s; typed N=5000 ~3.46 s, N=10000
~14.69 s. The untyped variant is now within ~17 % of the typed twin at N=5000
and within ~18 % at N=10000, and it is competitive with Python 3.14 (uv).
Correctness verified against upstream `julia` and the existing typed-loop
specialization regression fixtures.

### CallSpecializeI64Slots fast path directly in the main interpreter loop (Issue #10514)

Issue #10508 cached predecoded `I64FunctionBlock`s in the
`CallSpecializeI64Slots` handler, but the hot path still routed through the
full `dispatch_instr` → `execute_call` → `execute_call_specialize_i64_slots`
sequence. This change hoists the happy path into the main interpreter loop
(`Vm::run` and `Vm::run_until_frame_return_inner`) so a hot
`CallSpecializeI64Slots` / `CallSpecializeInboundsI64Slots` instruction checks
the direct `Vec` cache, loads small-arity `I64` arguments from typed slots,
and executes the cached block by reference without entering the generic call
dispatch machinery. On failure the instruction falls through to the unchanged
handler path, preserving all fallback semantics.

Result on `benchmarks/calc_pi_n5000.jl` (release-fast CLI, warm run): untyped
N=5000 improves from ~9.7 s to ~8.9 s (~8 %). The benchmark is dominated by
`mygcd(a,b)` calls that are already specialized; removing the extra dispatch
layer saves roughly one second on this workload. Correctness verified by
`calc_pi_6293_tests`, `regression_specialization_tests`, and the `loops::`
fixture category.

### stdlib macro (@test 等) の式/値位置 LOWERING 修正 (Issue #10293 解決 / #10307 部分)

`using Test` 後の `@test`/`@testset`/`@test_throws`/`@test_broken` を
代入 RHS・二項演算子オペランド (`@test(x) isa T` の隣接括弧スペリング含む)・
関数呼び出し引数などの式/値位置で **lowering** できるようにした
(#10293 解決)。式位置マクロディスパッチ
(`lowering/expr/macros/mod.rs`)のフォールバックに文位置と同じ
`has_stdlib_macro` 探索を追加し、新設 `expand_stdlib_macro_expr`
(`lowering/expr/macros/expand.rs`)で文位置と同一の静的 quote 展開エンジン
(`lowering::stmt::macros::expand::expand_stdlib_macro`)を再利用、返り値
`Stmt` を式化(`Stmt::Expr`→式そのもの、`Stmt::Block`→`Expr::LetBlock`)して
返す。fixture:
`tests/fixtures/macros/stdlib_macro_expr_position_10293_10307.jl`。詳細は
STATUS.md 参照。**#10307 は未解決のまま**: `@test` の値位置**返り値**が
`nothing` のままで upstream の `Test.Result`/`TestSet` オブジェクトにならない
値セマンティクス(#10307 の本題)は本 PR の範囲外。**別 Issue #10496 で追跡**
し、#10307 は #10496 が入るまで open。

### map/collect callable 型コンストラクタ結果の outer eltype 精緻化 (Issues #10187 / #10272 / #10250)

`map(Vector, [[1], [2]])` などコンテナ型コンストラクタを HOF に渡したときの
outer 配列要素型が upstream と一致するようになった:

- `typeof(map(Vector, [[1], [2]])) == Vector{Vector{Int64}}`
  (以前は `Vector{Array{Any, Any}}`)。
- `map(Matrix, …) == Vector{Matrix{…}}`、`map(Vector, [[1.0],[…]]) ==
  Vector{Vector{Float64}}`、`map(x->[x], …)` / `collect(Vector(x) for x in xs)`
  も同様に nested 型を保持。
- direct (`Vector(src)`) / callable (`map(Vector, [src])[1]`) / typed
  (`Vector{T}(src)`) が型・コピー semantics で一致することを検証。

実装は `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/hof_exec/value_mode.rs` の
`create_typed_array_from_values`。全要素が同一具体パラメトリック配列型の
array wrapper のとき、その型を outer 要素タグに採用する
(`value_mode_nested_array_element_type`)。空/scalar/異種要素は従来挙動維持。
fixture: `array/map_vector_ctor_outer_eltype_10187.jl`。

### struct nested in a module-body let/begin (Issue #10382); reject struct nested in a function's own let inside a macro-call-containing function (Issue #10402)

Two narrower gaps left after #10194's `lower_transparent_block_stmts` fix
(struct/mutable struct nested in a plain top-level `let`/`begin`, verified
against upstream `julia`):

- **#10382**: the same pattern *inside a `module ... end` body*
  (`module M; let; struct Foo; x::Int; end; ...; end; end`) still hit
  `UnsupportedFeature { kind: UnsupportedExpression("struct_definition") }`.
  Root cause: `lower_module_definition`'s statement-lowering catch-all
  (`lower_stmt_with_macro_ctx_if_needed` in `lowering/mod.rs`) only threaded
  the module's `LambdaContext` through when the statement itself contained a
  macro call (`contains_macro_call`), unlike Program/file top level's two
  entry points, which thread `Some(&lambda_ctx)` unconditionally. Every
  `lower_module_definition` call site passes a live context in practice, so
  dropping the `contains_macro_call` gate makes module-body statement
  lowering consistent with true top level rather than introducing new
  behavior. Fixture:
  `tests/fixtures/struct/nested_in_let_inside_module_10382.jl` (both `let`
  and `begin` forms, parity-checked).

- **#10402**: a `struct` nested inside a `let`/`begin` that is itself nested
  inside a **function body** must be rejected — upstream Julia rejects any
  `struct` not lexically at top level with `ERROR: LoadError: syntax:
  "struct" expression not at top level`. sjulia was silently accepting and
  running this when the enclosing function's own body also contained a
  macro call (routing it through the ctx-aware lowering path that also
  handles #10194's legal nesting). The issue's own "fix sketch" (calling the
  existing `reject_macro_expanded_structs_in_non_toplevel`, which drains the
  *whole* macro-expanded-struct queue) would have regressed a legal sibling
  program — e.g. `let; struct Good; x::Int; end; function f(); @show 1; end;
  end` queues `Good` first, then unconditionally rejecting on the non-empty
  queue while lowering `f` would incorrectly reject the whole program and
  drop `Good`. Fixed with a watermark/delta approach instead, mirroring the
  existing `lifted_function_count`/`lifted_functions_from_index` pattern:
  `LambdaContext::macro_expanded_struct_count()` snapshots the queue length
  before lowering a nested `FunctionDefinition`/`ShortFunctionDefinition`,
  and the new `take_macro_expanded_structs_from(start)` (`Vec::split_off`)
  plus `reject_macro_expanded_structs_added_since` only inspect/reject
  structs queued *after* that watermark, leaving earlier sibling entries
  untouched. Both the rejection MWE and the sibling-legal-program guard are
  covered by
  `integration_tests.rs::integration_struct_hof_tests::chunk_006`.

Issue #10401 (struct nested directly in a top-level `if`/`for`/`while`/`try`
body) remains open/unfixed: matching upstream's per-branch definedness (`if
false ... else ...` → only the taken branch's struct is ever defined,
`isdefined(Main, :FooIfA) == false`) is structurally incompatible with
sjulia's only existing mechanism (#10194's unconditional compile-time
hoist, which would define both branches' structs and diverge from
upstream). It needs a genuine runtime-conditional struct-definition
primitive (`Stmt::StructDef` + `isdefined` wiring) — a materially larger
feature than this lowering fix, deferred as its own follow-up.

### First-class parametric array constructors align with direct syntax (Issue #10405)

Fixed callable `DataType` dispatch for parametric constructors used as values:
`map(Vector{Int64}, xs)` now allocates fresh vectors instead of returning the
source by identity, `map(Vector{Float64}, xs)` converts element storage, and
`map(Array, xs)` / `map(Array{Float64}, xs)` route through Base constructor
methods instead of a runtime MethodError. The same runtime candidate + type
parameter binding path also covers `Matrix{T}` callable values.

The VM now augments callable `Value::DataType` candidate lookup with matching
parametric method names (`Vector{T}` for `Vector{Float64}`, etc.) and binds
the callable type's actual parameters into the selected method frame before
executing the body. Base `array.jl` gained constructor methods for
`Vector{T}(::AbstractVector)`, `Array(::AbstractVector/AbstractRange)`, and
`Array{T}(::AbstractVector/AbstractRange)`, keeping constructor copy semantics
separate from `convert(::Type{Vector{T}}, a)` identity semantics.

Expanded `tests/fixtures/array/ctor_direct_vs_callable_parity_10213.jl` to
assert same-eltype and converting `Vector{T}` callable paths, range sources,
bare/typed `Array`, and bare/typed/converting `Matrix` against upstream Julia.
While adding dotted-call coverage, found the separate lowering gap
`Vector{T}.(xs)` → `UnsupportedCallTarget` and filed Issue #10475; the fixture
references that gap and covers equivalent callable dispatch via
`broadcast(Vector{T}, xs)`.
The full-suite `@testset` ratchet also showed the allowlist row for the already
closed Issue #10447 had become stale; removed
`types/types_agg_value_params_10238.jl` from
`docs/vm/TESTSET_FAILURE_ALLOWLIST.tsv` and regenerated the derived tracker
body for Issue #9472.

Closes #10405; refs #10213, #10447, #10475, #9472.

### Semicolon-only and single-`;` scalar array literals (Issues #10379 / #10380)

Array-literal semicolon edge cases now match upstream Julia:

- `[;]` / `[;;]` / `[;;;]` lower as empty `Array{Any,N}` values, with
  rank equal to the semicolon count and shapes `(0,)`, `(0,0)`, `(0,0,0)`, ...
- `[1; 2; 3]` lowers as a rank-1 `Vector{Int64}`, not an `(N,1)` matrix.
  The typed scalar-chain form `Int64[1; 2; 3]` follows the same rank-1 shape.
- Higher-level separators still take the existing N-dimensional fold path:
  `[1;; 2;; 3]` remains a `(1,3)` `Matrix`.

Implementation: `lower_vector_expr_impl` recognizes all-semicolon empty
untyped literals; `lower_matrix_expr_impl` collapses pure single-`;` one-scalar
rows to rank 1 before the general `nd_fold`; `lower_typed_matrix_expr` now
allows rank-1 raw shapes so `T[1;2;3]` can produce a vector. Regression coverage
was added to `array/ncat_literal_ndim_shape_10190.jl`, extending the existing
#10190/#10378 fixture. A newly discovered adjacent gap for typed all-semicolon
empty literals (`Int64[;]`, `Int64[;;]`) is tracked separately as #10506.

### Retire the `EuclideanModuloI64Function` coprime-gcd special case (Issue #10310)

`EuclideanModuloI64Function` / `EuclideanModuloI64LoopBlock` was a dedicated
predecode recognizer + frame-less call-site shortcut hard-coded to exactly one
loop shape: `while b != 0; (a, b) = (b, a % b); end` (the coprime-π
benchmark's `mygcd`). Retired per owner directive (2026-07-11): the special
case inflated sjulia's apparent coprime-π performance relative to the general
typed-loop path, which is benchmark-gaming — the general path is now the
honest measurement. Removed `EuclideanModuloI64Loop`'s `ExecutableBlock`
variant, `recognize_euclidean_modulo_i64_loop`, `try_predecode_euclidean_modulo_i64_loop`,
`execute_euclidean_modulo_i64_loop_block`, `sync_euclidean_modulo_i64_slots`,
`euclidean_modulo_i64_function_arg_indices`, `execute_euclidean_modulo_i64_values`,
and the two call-site wrapper fns, plus their 3 call sites in
`vm/exec/call.rs`. `LOOP_RECOGNIZERS` drops from 3 entries to 2.

The coprime-gcd loop now runs through the general typed-loop machinery that
already existed: `TypedLoopOp::ModI64`/`LoadModI64Slot` (frame-based
`ExecutableBlock::Typed`) and the frame-less `I64FunctionBlock` call path
(`ExecutableBlock::I64Function`, built for Issue #10309's call-inlining work)
both already cover this shape — no new recognizer code was needed. Verified
via `SJULIA_VM_PROFILE=1`: `mygcd` calls now fire `ExecutableBlock::I64Function`
(previously `ExecutableBlock::EuclideanModuloI64Function`).

Correctness is unaffected — verified against `julia --startup-file=no`
(`fixtures/loops/loops_while_gcd_general_typed_loop_10310.jl`, parity-checked,
covers the `b == 0`/`a == 0` on-entry edge cases) and AoT (coprime-π is an AoT
acceptance kernel, but AoT's native codegen never used this VM-interpreter-only
code path, so it is unaffected either way; `test_aot.sh` reconfirmed).

Performance: this is a **deliberate, accepted regression** on the coprime-π
benchmark specifically (not a general slowdown — `TypedLoopOp`/`I64FunctionBlock`
already served every other typed loop). VM-only (`Vm::run()`, N=1000,
`benches/calc_pi_benchmark.rs`): 106ms → 247ms (≈2.3x). CLI (cache-embedded,
N=5000): 2.70s → 6.58s (≈2.4x); N=10000: 10.93s → 27.19s (≈2.5x). AoT and
upstream `julia` are unaffected (AoT ≈0.5s/≈2.2s, `julia` ≈0.67s/≈2.87s for
N=5000/N=10000). Honest general-path recovery is tracked separately (NOT
folded into #10310): #10297 (register VM coverage for this exact benchmark),
#10104/#10477 (typed-loop recognizer coverage), #10309 (typed call inlining
gate), #10439 (call-site specialization of untyped hot callees), #10102
(back-edge-only safepoint).

### Stack VM: memory-waterline safepoint moved to back-edges only (Issue #10102)

The struct-heap memory-waterline safepoint
(`check_memory_waterline_safepoint`, which triggers struct-heap compaction
when the soft limit is exceeded) was called after **every** instruction
dispatch (the `DispatchAction::Continue` path in `run()` and
`run_until_frame_return_inner`). It is now checked only at loop back-edges
(`jump_to`'s `target < self.ip` branch, alongside the existing back-edge
cancel check) and at `Call`/`Return`/`Print`/HOF boundaries (via
`handle_pending_call_depth_overflow`, which already carried the check),
removing one branch per loop-body instruction. This mirrors how cancel checks
already work (Call + back-edges only) and how the register VM checks every
4096 instructions.

**Container-return postlude symmetry.** The scalar `Return*` arms
(`Return{F64,F32,F16,I64,Array,Any,Nothing,Rng,Range,Ref}`) already carried the
`handle_pending_call_depth_overflow` postlude (which runs the waterline
safepoint), but the container returns
(`ReturnStruct`/`ReturnTuple`/`ReturnNamedTuple`/`ReturnDict`/`ReturnSet`) were
folded into their group arms and lacked it. A per-element HOF / broadcast /
generator driver whose callee returns a struct enters the callee *without* the
`Call` postlude (`push_hof_call_frame_with_generated` sets `self.ip` directly)
and returns via `ReturnStruct` — not a back-edge — so those container returns
must also carry the postlude to keep struct-heap growth bracketed by a
safepoint. They were split out of their group arms into dedicated postluded
arms, restoring symmetry with the scalar returns. The hot handler table does
not list container returns as hot rows, so they route through the shared
fallback into the same dispatch macro — one edit covers both dispatch paths.

**Correctness / honest detection lag.** Unbounded struct-heap growth must pass
through either a loop (back-edge → `jump_to`), recursion, or a call/return
boundary (→ `handle_pending_call_depth_overflow`); finite straight-line blocks
are bounded by program size and caught at the next boundary or executable-block
Exit. The real waterline check fires once per `MEMORY_WATERLINE_CHECK_INTERVAL`
(1024) safepoint invocations, so detection now lags by up to ~1024
back-edges/boundaries (≈ loop-body-length × 1024 allocations) instead of ~1024
instructions — the waterline does not need immediate reaction, so this lag is
acceptable, and detection still always fires. TypedLoop blocks keep their
existing block-exit compaction.

Verified: struct-per-iteration loops, struct-constructor broadcasts, and struct
comprehensions stay correct and still raise `OutOfMemory` cleanly under a tiny
`SJULIA_MEMORY_BUDGET_BYTES`, at peak RSS matching `main`; the 1000-iteration
long-session struct-heap-boundedness / compaction stress tests (#9787/#8625)
stay green. New regression fixtures
`struct/struct_alloc_loop_safepoint_10102.jl` and
`struct/struct_per_element_return_safepoint_10102.jl`. Benchmark (2M-iteration
struct hot loop, interleaved A/B min): before 10.71s → after 9.86s (~8%
faster). Incidental discovery while writing the fixture: broadcasting a
NamedTuple-returning function (`h.(1:n)`) runs upstream but failed in sjulia;
that follow-up was resolved later the same day in Issue #10469.

### VM helper consolidation: cmp_str / slot_out_of_bounds (Issue #10260, bounded subset)

Behavior-preserving DRY cleanup of two duplicated VM-execution patterns from
the Issue #10260 catalogue (A9, A8). No behavior change; the remaining ~519
catalogued sites stay open under #10260.

- **A9 — string comparison (`vm/exec/comparison.rs`)**: the five string
  comparison instructions (`EqStr`/`LtStr`/`LeStr`/`GtStr`/`GeStr`) each carried
  an identical ~10-line pop/guard/compare/push block differing only by operator.
  Factored into `Vm::cmp_str<F: Fn(&[u8], &[u8]) -> bool>` in `vm/state.rs`,
  mirroring the existing `cmp_i64`/`cmp_f64` helpers; each arm is now a one-line
  closure. Non-string operands still compare `false` (Issue #2025). Parity with
  upstream julia verified across equality/ordering/case/empty/common-prefix.
- **A8 — slot out-of-bounds (`vm/exec/locals.rs`, `jump.rs`, `call.rs`)**: ~51
  byte-identical `InternalError(format!("<Instr>: slot out of bounds: {}", slot))`
  blocks (differing only by instruction-name prefix) routed through a single
  `slot_out_of_bounds(instr, slot)` free function in `vm/exec/mod.rs` (beside the
  existing `unhandled` helper). `slot: impl Display` keeps each rendered message
  byte-identical; these are compiler-invariant paths, so no user-visible change.
- Net −150 lines. `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean; `match_same_arms`
  (a pedantic, non-gated lint used by #10260 only as a detection heuristic)
  count on touched files unchanged — these were code-duplication patterns, not
  lint hits.

### Stack VM: destructive slot load `TakeSlot` (move semantics) (Issue #10107)

Added a destructive slot-load instruction `TakeSlot(i)` that MOVES the value
out of local slot `i` (leaving `None`) instead of cloning it, avoiding a
`Value::clone` (`Rc` refcount bump / deep `Box`/`Vec` copy) for
reference-carrying return values. The peephole optimizer rewrites a plain
verbatim-clone `LoadSlot*(i); Return*` into `TakeSlot(i); Return*` in its
post-slotize pass.

The rewrite is guarded by a conservative, provably-sound last-use check and
fires only when ALL hold: (1) the load is a verbatim-clone slot load
(converting `LoadSlotI64ToF64` and scalar fast-path loads excluded); (2) the
next instruction is a value-consuming `Return*` (`ReturnNothing` excluded);
(3) the pair is strictly inside the function-body region (`k+1 < main_entry`)
— never the persistent main/global frame 0, which survives its `Return*` and
is read back by `Vm::get_global`; (4) no exception handler is active
(`PushHandler`/`PopHandler` nesting is zero at the load). Because the `Return*`
discards the frame immediately after the move, no later instruction of the
frame can observe the emptied slot except a `finally`/`catch`, which the
handler-nesting guard excludes. Independently reviewed by codex (no
counterexample found; structured-lowering precondition documented).

Scope / deferred (Issue #10107 stays open): the register VM has no `TakeSlot`
translation, so a function containing one stays on the stack VM (these are
trivial `LoadSlot*; Return*` leaf accessors where the register VM offers no
benefit). A general per-basic-block liveness analysis (rewriting non-adjacent
last uses, or under handlers with a proven safe range) is deferred.

Implementation: `subset_julia_vm_bytecode/src/{instr.rs,peephole.rs}`,
`subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/exec/{locals.rs,call.rs,mod.rs}`, `register_gate.rs`,
`profiler.rs`; `CACHE_VERSION` bumped 95→96 (`Instr` gained a tail-appended
variant). Tests: 10 peephole unit tests (fire / decline / adversarial) plus the
`functions/functions_destructive_load_10107.jl` fixture (heap accessors,
mutually-exclusive branch returns, and the adversarial declines — try/finally
reading the returned var, closure capture, aliasing escape — with upstream
`julia` parity).

### HOF / builtin per-element failures are now catchable (Issue #10406)

A builtin or higher-order-function per-element failure — `sqrt("a")` directly,
and per-element via `map(sqrt, xs)` / `sum(sqrt, xs)` — used to abort the whole
program with an uncatchable top-level `Runtime error: ...` instead of a
catchable Julia exception that a surrounding `try`/`catch` observes (upstream
raises a catchable `MethodError`). Root cause: the VM run loop's terminal error
arm (`Vm::run` in `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/exec/mod.rs`) returned bare-`?`-propagated
errors straight out of the loop without ever consulting the installed exception
handlers. Errors only became catchable when an instruction handler explicitly
called `self.raise()` (e.g. the `CallBuiltin`/`CallIntrinsic` arms); paths that
propagated with a plain `?` (the numeric fast paths' `value_to_f64` type check,
and the per-element callee failures surfaced by HOFs) leaked past the handler.

Fix: the terminal error arm now routes catchable errors through `self.raise()`
(mirroring the `CallBuiltin` arm), gated by the new
`Vm::is_catchable_vm_error` predicate so the six VM-internal / host-control
variants (`Cancelled`, `StackUnderflow`, `NotImplemented`, `InternalError`,
`UnknownBroadcastOp`, `InvalidInstruction`) stay uncatchable. The change is
monotonic — `raise` only catches when a handler is installed, so programs
without a surrounding `try` are unaffected — and does not touch
`run_until_frame_return_inner` (the #5972 eval-floor path, verified to already
route eval-internal `try`/`catch` correctly). Regression coverage:
`exceptions/catchable_hof_builtin_error_10406.jl` (parity-checked) plus three
`vm::tests` unit tests (predicate/None-set consistency, terminal-arm catch,
terminal-arm keeps internal errors uncatchable).

Note: the caught value is a `TypeError` (sjulia's numeric fast path) where
upstream raises a `MethodError`; the exact exception-type parity is a separate
refinement that needs the numeric fast path routed through the dispatch
resolver (Refs #10405, #10461). Closes #10406.

### Module-scope resolution qualified keying (Issues #10214 / #10236)

Two different modules (or a module and Main) defining a same-named nested
closure or `let`/`@testset`-root helper no longer collide. `module_scope_overrides`
is keyed by the helper's `inline_functions` collection index (not bare name);
`function_module_paths` is keyed by the module-qualified `"Module.path.func"`
and `collect_from_module` gives a module's nested children a module-qualified
parent identity. A module-body `let`/`@testset`-root helper is kept out of the
runtime bare short-name index (`FunctionInfo::suppress_short_name_alias`) so a
closure value created for an unrelated same-named Main-level `let` root cannot
resolve to the module's helper body. `callable_singleton_struct_name`
(subset_julia_vm_types) keeps `typeof(Module.func#anon)` recognized as
`<: Function` (fixes a latent `base_type_name` mangling exposed by the qualified
nested names; regression-guarded by the #7180 module-closure-HOF fixture).

Regression coverage: `modules/module_scope_qualified_keying_10214.jl` and
`modules/module_let_root_qualified_keying_10236.jl` (upstream parity-checked),
plus the full `modules::` category and the pre-existing #7180 / #10073 fixtures.
Residual same-scope-two-lets case tracked as #10395; unrelated module-scope
`Ref` coercion as #10363; design/prevention epic #10243.

### Value-carried container differential corpus (Issue #9793)

Added `repl_differential/value_carried_containers_9793.toml` and a dedicated
`differential_value_carried_container_ops_corpus_9793` gate to keep the #9786
class covered in the Legacy-vs-Persistent REPL differential harness. The corpus
defines Tuple, NamedTuple, and Pair globals in one eval, then consumes them in
later evals through destructuring, positional indexing, `first`/`last`,
`collect`, `sum`, and positional splat where the surface is currently supported.

Tuple, NamedTuple, and Pair now cover the full requested operation set;
#10476 supplied the remaining Pair iterator-like operations (`last`, `collect`,
`sum`, and splat), so the same differential corpus now guards them across eval
boundaries. Closes #9793; refs #9786, #10476.

### struct definitions nested in a macro-expanded/let/begin block (Issue #10194)

A `struct`/`mutable struct` definition nested inside `Test.@testset "..."
begin ... end` (or a plain top-level `let ... end`, a bare top-level
`begin ... end`, `x = begin ... end`, or a user-defined macro that re-emits
its caller-supplied body via `esc(body)`) now lowers and runs, matching
upstream Julia — these constructs are "transparent" wrappers that execute
unconditionally exactly once, so a nested struct is legal there whenever the
wrapper itself is reachable from top level (upstream Julia only rejects
`struct` lexically inside a function/closure body). Previously this failed
to lower with `UnsupportedFeature { kind:
UnsupportedExpression("struct_definition") }`.

Root cause (two independent bugs on the same call path):

1. `NodeKind::StructDefinition`/`MutableStructDefinition` had no handling in
   the "begin/let block treated as an expression or as a `let`/RHS body"
   lowering helpers (`lower_expr_with_ctx`'s `NodeKind::Block` arm,
   `lower_let_expr[_with_ctx]`, and the dedicated `x = begin ... end`
   identifier-assignment path from Issue #7617) — they iterated block
   children calling `lower_stmt`/`lower_stmt_with_ctx` directly, which falls
   through to the ordinary expression-lowering catch-all for a struct node.
   New shared helper `lower_transparent_block_stmts`
   (`subset_julia_vm_lowering/src/lowering/stmt/mod.rs`) intercepts a direct
   `struct`/`mutable struct` child, lowers it via
   `struct_::lower_struct_definition`, and registers it through the existing
   macro-expanded-struct queue (Issue #7915) instead of trying to represent
   it as a `Stmt` (there is no `Stmt::StructDef` variant). Deliberately
   *not* wired into `if`/`for`/`while`/`try`/function/closure body lowering,
   which keep their current (correct) rejection — a function/closure body is
   genuinely illegal upstream, but `if`/`for`/`while`/`try` are actually
   *legal* upstream (verified: `for i in 1:1; struct Foo; x::Int; end; end`,
   `while`, and `try`/`catch` all define the struct upstream, same as `if`),
   just execution-conditional/repeated rather than unconditional-once —
   unconditionally hoisting a nested struct out of one of those bodies the
   way this fix does for `begin`/`let` would be wrong runtime semantics, not
   just an unsupported case (an `if`/`else` with different struct names in
   each branch only defines the *taken* branch's struct upstream).
   Faithfully supporting `if`/`for`/`while`/`try` needs a genuine runtime
   struct-definition statement, a materially larger feature tracked
   separately as Issue #10401; Issue #10382 covers the narrower
   `module`-body residual gap for the `begin`/`let` case this PR does fix.
2. Once (1) stopped the lowering-time crash, the queued struct still had to
   reach `Program.structs` — `LoweringWithInclude::lower` (the file/CLI
   lowering entry point used by `sjulia <file>.jl`) never called
   `drain_macro_expanded_structs`/`drain_macro_expanded_macros` in its
   generic statement catch-all, `ConstStatement` arm, or non-`include()`
   `CallExpression` arm, unlike `Lowering::lower` (the `-e`/REPL-fragment
   entry point) and `lower_module_definition` (module bodies), which already
   drained correctly. Without the drain, a queued struct's constructor
   silently resolved as `Unknown function: <Name>` at runtime instead of
   erroring at lowering — same symptom as the pre-existing user-defined-macro
   constructor bug (Issue #10370), which this drain fix also resolves as a
   side effect (it shares the same root cause).
   `FunctionDefinition`/`ShortFunctionDefinition` arms in
   `LoweringWithInclude::lower` also gained the matching
   `reject_macro_expanded_structs_in_non_toplevel` safety-net call (already
   present in `Lowering::lower`) so a struct wrongly queued while lowering a
   nested function's body is rejected instead of silently draining into
   `Program.structs`.

Regression coverage: `macros/testset_nested_struct_def_10194.jl`,
`macros/user_macro_quote_nested_struct_10194.jl`,
`struct/nested_in_let_top_level_10194.jl`,
`struct/nested_in_begin_assignment_rhs_10194.jl`.

### N-dimensional `;`/`;;`/`;;;`/... array-literal shape folding (Issues #10190, #10378)

A `[...]` array literal using Julia's `;;`/`;;;`/`;;;;`/... dimension-
separator syntax (`N` consecutive semicolons concatenate along dimension
`N`) was mis-shaped: the parser collapsed every semicolon/newline run into a
single "next row" boundary regardless of how many semicolons it contained,
so e.g. `[1 2; 3 4;;; 5 6; 7 8]` (upstream `Array{Int64,3}`, size `(2,2,2)`)
lowered to a `Matrix{Int64}` of size `(4,2)`.

- `subset_julia_vm_parser`: `Parser::consume_row_separator_run` (shared by
  `parse_matrix_rest`/`parse_matrix_row_rest` in `collections.rs` and the
  typed-matrix counterparts in `expressions/index.rs`) now emits one
  `Semicolon` CST leaf per `;` token in a separator run instead of silently
  discarding the count, preserving each run's dimension level.
- `subset_julia_vm`: `lower_matrix_expr_impl` (`lowering/expr/collection.rs`)
  folds the recorded levels via a new `nd_fold`/`nd_cat` pair that merges
  row-blocks strictly by increasing separator level (mirroring upstream's
  `cat(...; dims = N)` semantics), computing both the correct N-dimensional
  shape and the correct column-major element order; mismatched shapes at any
  level are a compile-time `MalformedMatrix` error. The typed-literal path
  (`T[...]`, `lower_typed_matrix_expr` in `lowering/expr/mod.rs`) now passes
  every recovered dimension through to `reshape`, not just `rows`/`cols`,
  so `T[1 2; 3 4;;; 5 6; 7 8]` also produces a genuine `Array{T,3}`.
- Issue #10378 (found alongside #10190): a *trailing* dangling separator
  with no following row (`[1 2;;;]`, accepted without erroring since Issue
  #8759) now pads the final shape with trailing size-1 dimensions instead of
  being dropped, matching upstream (`size([1 2;;;]) == (1, 2, 1)`, not
  `(1, 2)`).

Regression coverage: `array/ncat_literal_ndim_shape_10190.jl` (MWE, a 3-page
`;;;` literal, a 4-D `;;;;` literal, an explicit `;;` dim-2 literal, a
level-skipping `;`+`;;;` literal, the typed-literal path, trailing-separator
padding, and 1-D/2-D regression checks — all verified against upstream
`julia` first) plus `lowering::expr::collection::tests::test_nd_fold_*` /
`test_nd_cat_*` unit tests for the fold/cat algorithm directly.

Adjacent gaps found during this investigation: #10379/#10380 are now fixed
(see the 2026-07-11 semicolon-literal entry above). Remaining separate gaps:
#10381 (N-D array literals with non-scalar/array-valued blocks, e.g.
`[A B; C D;;; ...]`, have no runtime `hvncat` and still mis-shape), #10385
(`println`/`show` of any rank-≥3 `Array` prints an internal `MemoryRef`
representation instead of upstream's nested literal form), and #10506 (typed
all-semicolon empty literals).

### `Base.infer_effects` ternary/short-circuit `terminates` over-claim fixed (Issue #10368)

`Base.infer_effects(f, types)` reported `terminates = true` (plus
`noub`/`nonoverlayed`/`nortcall`) for a call (e.g. `println`) reachable
only through `Expr::Ternary` (`cond ? a : b`) or short-circuit `&&`/`||`,
while correctly reporting `terminates = false` (matching upstream `julia
1.12.6`) for the SAME call at top level, inside an `if`/`elseif`/`else`
block, or a loop — distinct from Issue #10145/#10264 (a
registration-eligibility gap for fully-typed-param methods, whose test
only asserted the already-correct `nothrow`/`effect_free` bits).

Root cause: the shared function-body effect walker
(`subset_julia_vm_types/src/runtime_types/function_effects.rs`
`compute_expr_effects`) resolves an unresolved callee (absent from this
program's `effects_map`, e.g. a Base Rust builtin excluded from the
whole-program propagation slice) to the fully conservative
`Effects::arbitrary()` when the call sits directly in statement position
(a bare call, or inside an `if`/`elseif`/`else` branch) — but a call nested
inside `Expr::Ternary` or short-circuit `Expr::BinaryOp{And,Or}` was routed
through the `infer_expr_effects_with_callees` bridge instead, whose own
missing-callee fallback consults the curated builtin name table
(`infer_builtin_effects`), which classifies
`println`/`print`/`show`/`display`/`write` as `Effects::with_side_effects()`
— optimistically claiming `terminates = true`.

Fix: `compute_expr_effects` now has dedicated arms for `Expr::Ternary` and
short-circuit `Expr::BinaryOp{And,Or}` that recurse through
`compute_expr_effects` itself (mirroring `Stmt::If`'s
condition/then_branch/else_branch composition), so a nested call resolves
via the same `effects_map` lookup as a bare statement call or an if/else
branch. The curated-name-table fallback for calls nested in ordinary
(non-control-flow) operator operands (Issue #8441's intentional behavior,
e.g. `string(x) + 1` staying foldable) is unchanged. Since this walker is
shared by both compile-time whole-program propagation and runtime
reflection, the fix also corrects the underlying `Effects` summary consumed
by CSE/DCE for these constructs, not just the `Base.infer_effects` display.

Added `tests/fixtures/reflection/infer_effects_ternary_shortcircuit_terminates_10368.jl`
(parity-verified against upstream `julia --startup-file=no`; asserts
`ternary`/`&&`/`||` forms produce the exact same `Base.infer_effects` output
as an equivalent if/else control via `string(ef)`) and a Rust unit test
`compile::effects::propagation::tests::ternary_and_short_circuit_missing_callee_match_if_else_terminates_issue_10368`.

### Base duplicate same-signature definitions audit (Issue #10185)

Added a prevention gate for the #10089 `invperm` class: duplicate
same-name/same-signature bundled Base definitions now have to be classified in
`docs/vm/BASE_DUPLICATE_SIGNATURE_ALLOWLIST.tsv`. The new
`scripts/check_base_duplicate_signatures.sh` audit scans
`subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/` with a conservative parser for long-form and
short-form Julia method definitions, normalizes untyped parameters to `Any`,
keeps `where` bounds, and fails on both unclassified duplicate groups and
stale allowlist rows. The initial allowlist classifies the current 30 duplicate
groups, with `invperm(Any)` tied back to #10089 and the rest to the #10185
baseline review.

Registered the audit in `docs/vm/CODE_AUDITS.md` and added a negative
self-test to `scripts/check_audit_negative_selftest.sh` that injects an
unclassified duplicate Base method and requires the new audit to fail with the
injected signature. While wiring this in, the existing #10279 name-based
lookup negative self-test was repaired to inject enough name-keyed TypeVar maps
to exceed its ratchet even after the clean tree has fallen below baseline, and
`audit_native_boundary_ccall.sh` was annotated as non-source-injectable for the
audit completeness check. Closes #10185; refs #10089, #10279, #9570.

### Range and array equality prevention checklists closed (Issues #10112, #10070, #10356)

Added durable checklist gates for three milestone 64 prevention items:

- Native range exact storage / internal counters (#10112): BigInt range public
  APIs must preserve exact endpoint/accessor/length semantics, while counted
  loops and allocation paths convert only at private Int-sized boundaries or
  fall back to generic `iterate`.
- Narrow-float range visible surfaces (#10070): Float16/Float32 range changes
  must verify `typeof`, `eltype`, `step`, accessors, `collect`, and
  `StepRangeLen{T,R,S,L}` dispatch keys together.
- Array `==` versus `isequal` fallback semantics (#10356): readable array `==`
  stays on value equality / `TupleEquals`, while `isequal` stays on its own
  bridge so signed-zero, NaN, and mixed exact/float cases do not collapse.

The checklists point to the existing regression fixtures and unit gates:
`range/bigint_endpoint_9420.jl`,
`range/float16_float32_colon_type_params_10019.jl`,
`comparison/dynamic_array_bigint_equality_9516.jl`,
`complex/complex_array_eq_carrier_5789.jl`,
`derive_range_element_type_tests`, and `test_value_enum_size_is_compact`.

### Native boundary ADR and upstream ccall ledger (Issue #9570)

Accepted `docs/vm/NATIVE_BOUNDARY.md` as the native-boundary ADR for the
mandatory WASM+iOS target set. User-visible arbitrary `ccall`, `@cfunction`,
`dlopen`, and raw pointer APIs remain unsupported by design; upstream native
surfaces may enter sjulia only as Policy A (Pure Rust / VM intrinsic /
curated host wrapper), Policy B (dual-compiled C/C++ library, requiring a
separate ADR plus iOS and WASM build evidence), or Policy C (documented
divergence/unsupported boundary). The initial generated ledger has no
Policy-B rows.

Added `scripts/audit_native_boundary_ccall.sh` and the line-level generated
`docs/vm/NATIVE_BOUNDARY_CCALL_LEDGER.tsv` for upstream Julia `base/` and
`stdlib/` `ccall` sites. The initial snapshot classifies 958 Policy-A rows
and 285 Policy-C rows, with explicit family decisions for Julia runtime
primitives, OS/libuv/IO wrappers, memory/string and Unicode helpers,
BigInt/GMP, BigFloat/MPFR (#9290), Regex/PCRE2 (#8992), libm/LLVM
intrinsics, Random/dSFMT (#8998), LibGit2/Pkg, dynamic loading,
user-native boundary syntax, shared-memory surfaces, docs/examples, and
upstream test-only calls. This turns future upstream `ccall` additions or
moves into a reviewable ledger diff.
Closes #9570; refs #9290, #8992, #8998.

### try/catch tail-position value semantics locked in (Issue #10254)

Design/prevention close-out for the concrete bug fixed in Issue #10074
(`try/catch` whose branches ended in a plain/op/global assignment silently
returned `nothing` or crashed instead of the assigned value). Re-verified a
broad matrix of MWEs (assign-only branches, rvalue vs. function-tail
position, `try`/`finally` without `catch`, nested try/catch, a bound catch
variable, typed post-use via arithmetic/`typeof`/string-concat/`::T` return
annotations, `global` assignment tails) against upstream `julia
--startup-file=no` — all 15/15 match on current `main`, confirming the
#10074 fix is a **structural** lowering rule, not an accidental narrow
patch: `try_stmt_into_value_expr`/`if_stmt_into_value_expr`
(`lowering/expr/mod.rs`) rewrite a tail-position `try`/`if` into a
value-producing `Expr::LetBlock` via the shared `assign_block_tail_value`
helper (which now has arms for `Stmt::Assign`/`Stmt::AddAssign` in addition
to the pre-existing `Stmt::Expr`/`Stmt::Try`/`Stmt::If`/`Stmt::Block` arms),
`finally_block` is left untouched by the rewrite so it structurally cannot
produce the result, and `compile_block_value`'s (`compile/expr/mod.rs`)
matching assign-tail arm gives `begin ... end` blocks the same behavior.
Return-type inference (`infer_block_branch` in
`compile/abstract_interp/engine/mod.rs`, the `Stmt::Try` arms in
`compile/inference.rs`) independently joins the branch tail types so
callers see the correct static type.

Added `tests/fixtures/exceptions/try_catch_tail_value_semantics_10254.jl`
(19 `@testset` blocks / 20 `@test` assertions, sjulia/upstream `julia` parity verified via
`scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`) covering the gaps not already exercised
by the narrower existing fixtures (`try_catch_expression_4784.jl`,
`nested_try_catch_expression_4833.jl`, `try_implicit_return_6223.jl`,
`try_catch_type_inference_9131.jl`,
`try_tail_assign_implicit_return_10074.jl`): assign-only tails at
rvalue/expression position (not just function-tail position), nested
try/catch with assign-only tails, catch-var binding + assign tail,
`try`/`finally` without `catch` with an assign-only tail, and typed
post-use of an assign-tail result. Documented the full value-semantics
rule set and mechanism in `docs/vm/LOWERING.md` ("`try`/`catch`/`finally`
as an Expression: Tail-Position Value Semantics") and the return-type-join
half in `docs/vm/TYPE_SYSTEM.md` ("`try`/`catch`/`finally` Tail-Position
Return-Type Join"). Closes #10254; refs #10074.

### Generalize assignment-statement tail-position value propagation to every shape (Issue #10431)

Verifying the #10254 close-out surfaced that the "an assignment is an
expression" rule was implemented only for `Stmt::Assign`/`Stmt::AddAssign`
(Issue #10074) — `v[i] = x` (`Stmt::IndexAssign`), `obj.field = x`
(`Stmt::FieldAssign`), `d[k] = x` (`Stmt::DictAssign`), and tuple
destructuring (`(a, b) = rhs`) still silently returned `nothing` (or the
wrong value) in tail position, and NOT just inside try/catch — the
identical gap reproduced in a plain function-body tail, an `if`/`else`
branch tail, and a bare `begin ... end` block tail.

Fixed generally across **four independent compilation backends** that each
separately implement "the last statement of a block is its value":
1. **Lowering rewrite** (`lowering/expr/mod.rs`): `assign_block_tail_value`
   gained a shared `split_assign_stmt_via_temp` arm for
   `IndexAssign`/`FieldAssign`/`DictAssign` — bind the RHS to a fresh
   `__sjvm_tail_assign_tmp_<span>` temporary, store using the temporary (so
   the RHS/index expressions are each evaluated exactly once), then read
   the temporary as the result. `compile_block_value`
   (`compile/expr/mod.rs`) and `compile_function_body`/
   `compile_block_with_implicit_return` (`compile/stmt.rs`) got the
   matching codegen arm.
2. **Return-type inference** (`compile/abstract_interp/engine/mod.rs`):
   `infer_block_branch`'s per-statement loop needed matching arms — without
   them the declared return type stayed `Nothing` while the (now-fixed)
   compiled body correctly returned the RHS value, which doesn't just print
   wrong, it **crashes** the caller's type-specific instruction (e.g.
   `PrintI64NoNewline` fed an actual `Nothing`). This layer's own CFG fast
   paths (`try_infer_straightline_cfg_return`/
   `cfg_authoritative_statement_value`) needed the identical fix
   independently, since they bypass the general loop when eligible.
3. **Lazy call-site specializer** (`vm/specialize/stmt.rs`): a THIRD,
   independent compiled representation (`CallSpecialize`, produced per call
   site once the declared return type is known) has its own
   `compile_function_body`/`compile_block_with_implicit_return` and needed
   the same fix, reusing the shared `split_assign_stmt_via_temp` helper.
   This backend is what turned the mismatch into an actual runtime crash —
   the interpreter path alone would have stayed silently wrong.

**Tuple destructuring**: `(a, b) = rhs` never lowers to the dedicated
`Stmt::DestructuringAssign` IR variant (vestigial, reachable only via
macro/`@eval`-evaluated quoted code) — `lower_tuple_destructuring_impl`
always decomposes it into a flat `Stmt::Block` of per-target
`Stmt::Assign`s. Fixed for the two sub-shapes that route the value through
