### Array literal splat `[a, v..., b]` lowering ✅ (Issue #4793)

- `[10, v..., 20]` (with `v = [1, 2, 3]`) failed at lowering
  with `UnsupportedExpression("splat_expression")`. Splat
  already worked in tuple literals and function calls; only
  array literals were missing.
- Fix:
  `lowering/expr/collection.rs::lower_vector_expr_impl` now
  detects `NodeKind::SplatExpression` children. When any
  splat is present, the vector literal is rewritten into a
  `vcat(...)` call: splat operands pass through unchanged,
  non-splat operands are wrapped in a 1-element
  `ArrayLiteral([elem])`. `vcat(args...)` (the existing
  varargs body in `base/array.jl`) flattens them with
  `promote_type` semantics, matching Julia's `[a, v..., b]`
  output exactly (element values and element type).
- Coverage: vector splat (middle/start/end/lone/multiple),
  scalar interleave, tuple splat, range splat, empty splat,
  Float promotion. Verified with
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh` against upstream julia.
- New fixture `array_literal_splat_4793` (10 testsets, 11
  assertions). 2700/2700 fixture and unit tests pass, clippy
  0 warnings.

### Vector(::AbstractRange) materializes (first slice) ✅ (Issue #4810)

- `Vector(1:3)` returned the range unchanged
  (`UnitRange{Int64}`) instead of materializing to a
  `Vector{Int64}`. Same for any range arg.
- Root cause: `compile_array_constructor` in
  `compile/expr/collection.rs` had a placeholder "compile the
  arg and return it" for the single-arg `Vector(arr)` form —
  fine as a no-op for actual arrays but wrong for ranges,
  where Julia's constructor materializes via `collect`.
- Fix:
  - In `compile_array_constructor`: when the single arg infers
    as a Range (`JuliaType::UnitRange` / `StepRange` /
    `AbstractRange` or `ValueType::Range`) AND no type args
    were given, emit
    `Instr::CallBuiltin(BuiltinId::RangeCollect, 1)` instead
    of the no-op placeholder.
  - Added `Vector(r::AbstractRange) = collect(r)` and
    `Vector{T}(r::AbstractRange) where {T}` (manual loop —
    splat in array literal `T[r...]` isn't supported yet,
    #4793) in `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/array.jl` for the
    Pure-Julia dispatch path.
- New fixture `array_vector_range_constructor_4810` (6
  assertions, three testsets) covers `Vector(1:3)`,
  `Vector(1:0.5:3)` (Float), and `Vector(::Array)` regression
  guard.
- Scope: first slice (no-type-args form). The typed form
  `Vector{Float64}(1:3)` still hits the compile intercept
  before reaching the Pure-Julia method; tracked as #4811.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float16 print uses scientific notation (closes #4802 / #4804 fix family) ✅ (Issue #4807)

- Third member of the #4802 / #4804 fix family: Float16 print
  didn't switch to scientific notation for large magnitudes.
  Surfaced by the parity probe extension from PR #4806/#4808
  (the Float16 cell exposed the divergence).
- Fix: `format_float16_julia`
  - Lowered the whole-number fixed-form upper bound from `1e5`
    to `1e3` to match Julia's F16 switchover threshold (narrower
    than F32/F64 because F16's max magnitude is only ~6.5e4).
  - Added a scientific arm for `|x|` outside `[1e-4, 1e3)` that
    uses a round-trip mantissa search via Rust's `{:.*e}` to
    find the shortest faithful form (F16 has only ~3.3 decimal
    digits of precision so the loop exits in 0–4 iterations).
- New fixture `numeric_float16_scientific_4807` (14 assertions,
  four testsets) covers small/large F16 scientific, the
  threshold boundary (`999.0` vs `1000.0` → `1.0e3`),
  normal-range regression, and special values.
- Parity probe now down from 4 → 3 divergences (the F16 cell
  passes; remaining 3 are #4779 multi-variable comprehension
  shape).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float32 print also uses scientific notation (follow-up to #4802) ✅ (Issue #4804)

- `format_float32_julia` had the same fall-through to Rust's
  default `Display` as `format_float_julia` did before PR #4803.
  `Float32(1.5e-10)` printed as `0.00000000015` instead of
  `1.5e-10`. PR #4803 (#4802) only touched the Float64 helper.
- Fix:
  - Lowered the whole-number fixed-form upper bound in
    `format_float32_julia` from `1e7` to `1e6` (matching the
    Float64 threshold).
  - Routed magnitudes outside `[1e-4, 1e6)` through a new
    `format_float32_scientific_julia` helper that calls Rust's
    `{:e}` on the f32 directly (not after `as f64` cast), so
    the printed mantissa reflects f32's shortest round-trip
    rather than the wider f64 form. Both scientific helpers
    now share a `julia_scientific_postprocess` helper for the
    `1e10` → `1.0e10` `.0` insertion.
- New fixture `numeric_float32_scientific_4804` (18 assertions,
  five testsets) covers the scientific notation for small/large
  Float32 magnitudes, regression guards for the normal range,
  threshold boundary checks, and special values.
- Float16 still uses its own round-tripping algorithm; not
  affected by this fix (the F16 magnitude range is narrower so
  the issue surfaces less often).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float64 print uses scientific notation matching Julia ✅ (Issue #4802)

- `print` / `string` / `repr` of `Float64` never used scientific
  notation in sjulia. Upstream switches to scientific for very
  small / very large magnitudes (e.g. `1.5e-10`, `1.0e308`);
  sjulia printed full decimal form, producing 300+ digit output
  for `floatmin(Float64)` / `floatmax(Float64)`.
- Concrete divergences (now fixed): `1.5e-10` (was
  `0.00000000015`), `1.5e20` (was 21-digit decimal),
  `floatmin(Float64)` (was 308-digit decimal), `floatmax(Float64)`
  (was 308-digit decimal), `2.5e15` (was `2500000000000000`).
- Fix:
  - Lowered the whole-number fixed-form upper bound in
    `format_float_julia` from `1e15` to `1e6` so values like
    `1.0e6` correctly route to scientific.
  - Added a scientific arm: if `|x|` is outside `[1e-4, 1e6)`
    (and non-zero), route through new
    `format_float_scientific_julia` helper. The helper uses
    Rust's `{:e}` then post-processes whole-mantissa cases
    (`1e10` → `1.0e10`) to match Julia's required `.0`
    convention.
- New fixture `numeric_float_scientific_4802` (22 assertions,
  five testsets) covers the scientific notation for very small
  and very large magnitudes, regression guards for the normal
  fixed-point range (`0.0`, `0.5`, `3.14`, `150000.0`,
  `0.0001`), threshold boundary checks (`1e-4` vs `1e-5`,
  `1e5` vs `1e6`), and special values (`NaN`, `Inf`, `-Inf`,
  `-0.0`).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green;
  parity probe still 3 known divergences (all #4779), no new
  ones introduced.

### angle(z::Complex{Int}) accepted (was Complex{Float64}-only) ✅ (Issue #4800)

- `angle(1 + 1im)` (a `Complex{Int64}`) failed at compile time
  with `Dispatch(NoMethodFound { name: "angle", arg_types:
  [Struct("Complex{Int64}")] })`. The Pure-Julia
  `angle(z::Complex{Float64})` was the only method, so
  Complex-typed-Int instances didn't resolve.
- Fix: widened the signature to
  `angle(z::Complex{T}) where {T<:Real}` in
  `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/complex.jl`, mirroring upstream
  `Base.angle(z::Complex) = atan(imag(z), real(z))`.
- New fixture `complex_angle_complex_4800` (6 assertions, two
  testsets) asserts `angle(1 + 1im)`, `angle(-1 + 0im)`,
  `angle(0 - 1im)`, `angle(3 + 4im)` (Complex{Int64}) and a
  Complex{Float64} regression guard.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, audits green.

### Feature-branch guard for /auto-work workflow ✅ (Issue #4798)

- Prevention for the direct-to-main commit pattern: during the
  #4795 work in this session, the agent forgot to create a
  feature branch first and committed on local `main`. Recovered
  before push (via `git branch fix/4795-... && git reset --hard
  origin/main && git checkout fix/4795-...`) so no remote damage,
  but the workflow rule violation surfaced the gap.
- Added `scripts/branch_guard.sh` — fails fast when the current
  git branch is `main` or `master`, with recovery instructions
  in the error message. Install as a `.git/hooks/pre-commit`
  hook to make the next direct-to-main commit impossible at
  the git layer:
  ```
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexec bash scripts/branch_guard.sh --quiet\n' > .git/hooks/pre-commit
  chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
  ```
- Naming: intentionally NOT `check_*.sh` because it's a
  developer-side guard, not a CI gate (same convention as
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh` and
  `scripts/probe_base_api_parity.sh`).
- Added "Feature-branch guard for `/auto-work`" bullet to
  `docs/vm/CODE_AUDITS.md` documenting the script, the hook
  install one-liner, and the recovery sequence.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, shellcheck clean, audits green.

### Char range 'a':'e' (first slice — construction/[i]/collect) ✅ (Issue #4795)

- `'a':'e'` (Char range, upstream `StepRange{Char, Int}`) used to
  crash on construction because `Instr::MakeRangeLazy` called
  `pop_f64_or_i64` which rejects `Value::Char` operands.
- Fix slice:
  - Added `RangeElementType::Char` variant to
    `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/value/range.rs`. `typed_element`
    converts the stored Unicode codepoint back to a `Char` via
    `char::from_u32` (with U+FFFD fallback for safety).
  - Added `Vm::pop_f64_or_i64_or_char` helper in `vm/mod.rs`;
    `Instr::MakeRangeLazy` uses it and tags the resulting
    `RangeValue` with `RangeElementType::Char` when any operand
    is a Char.
  - `RangeValue::collect` Char arm builds a `Vector{Char}` via
    `char::from_u32` per element.
  - `Range[i]` (the array_index Range path) routes Char ranges
    through `typed_element` instead of the Int64-narrowing
    branch, returning Char values from indexing.
  - `eltype(::Range{Char})` arm + iterator element-type arm
    added so reflection sees Char.
- New fixture `numeric_char_range_4795` (10 assertions, five
  testsets) covers `length`, `[i]`, `collect`, `first`, `last`
  for `'a':'e'`, plus numeric range regression guards.
- Scope: this is the first slice. The for-loop iteration path
  (`for c in 'a':'e'`) still binds the loop variable as `Int64`
  because the specialized for-range instruction bypasses
  `typed_element` — tracked as a follow-up under #4796.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Float64 whole-number range preserves Float at first/[i] ✅ (Issue #4760)

- `0.0:1.0:5.0` (and other Float64 ranges with whole-number
  endpoints) silently narrowed `first` / `last` / `step` / `[i]`
  to `Int64`. `repr(0.0:1.0:5.0)` returned `"0:1:5"` (dropping
  the `.0`), so eval-roundtrips landed in `UnitRange{Int}`
  instead of `StepRangeLen{Float64}`. Same type-preservation
  family as #4745 (negative zero).
- Root cause: the range `getindex` heuristic at
  `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/exec/array_index.rs` narrowed any
  computed element with `fract() == 0.0` to `Int64`,
  regardless of the range's `is_float` flag. Both `first(r)`
  (via Pure-Julia `first(arr) = arr[1]`) and direct `r[i]`
  routed through this path.
- Fix: the narrowing branch now also requires `!range.is_float`.
  Non-float ranges keep their existing behavior (so
  `(1:5)[1] === Int64(1)` still holds); float ranges route
  through `range.typed_element(element)` which preserves the
  Float64 element type.
- New fixture `numeric_range_index_float_4760` (17 assertions,
  five testsets) covers `repr` / `first` / `last` / `step` /
  `[i]` / `collect` for whole-number Float64 ranges, with
  regression guards for the Int range path and the
  non-whole-step Float range path.
- Added a regression guard probe to
  `scripts/probe_base_api_parity.sh` (probes 59 total, still
  3 known divergences all #4779).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

- Prevention for the fix family #4785 / #4787 / #4789 — all three

### abs(typemin(IntN)) for narrow signed integers no longer crashes ✅ (Issue #4789)

- `abs(typemin(IntN))` for N < 64 (Int8/Int16/Int32) crashed with
  `Type error: Cannot negate "I8(-128)"` instead of returning
  `typemin(IntN)` itself. Upstream Julia silently returns the same
  value because two's-complement arithmetic wraps:
  `-typemin(IntN) == typemin(IntN)` for any signed N-bit integer.
- Root cause: Pure-Julia `abs(x::Int64) = flipsign(x, x)` handled
  the Int64 case correctly, but narrow signed integers fell
  through to the generic `abs(x) = -x if signbit(x) else x` in
  `julia/base/number.jl`, which routed through `dynamic_neg` whose
  narrow-integer arms were missing.
- Fix: `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/dynamic_ops/mod.rs::dynamic_neg`
  now uses `wrapping_neg` for all signed integer widths
  (I8/I16/I32/I64/I128), matching upstream's two's-complement
  semantics. Float/Bool/BigInt/BigFloat arms unchanged.
- New fixture `numeric_abs_typemin_narrow_4789` (17 assertions,
  four testsets) covers `abs(typemin(IntN))` for N ∈ {8,16,32,64,
  128}, normal narrow-integer abs (regression guards), the
  underlying `-typemin(IntN)` primitive, and Float/Bool negation
  regression guards.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### bswap respects element bit width (follow-up to #4785) ✅ (Issue #4787)

- Same root cause family as #4785: `bswap` for non-Int64 integer
  types returned wrong results because the compile path coerced
  the argument to I64 and the runtime arm byte-swapped all 8
  bytes regardless of original width. PR #4786 fixed
  count_zeros / leading_* / bitreverse but `bswap` was left
  behind.
- Fix:
  - `subset_julia_vm_compile/src/compile/expr/builtin_math.rs` —
    `"bswap"` arm uses plain `compile_expr` and returns the
    expr's actual type rather than forcing I64.
  - `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/builtins_math.rs` — `BuiltinId::Bswap`
    arm pops a `Value`, match-dispatches over every integer
    variant (I8/16/32/64/128, U8/16/32/64/128), and pushes the
    original variant back.
- New fixture `numeric_bswap_width_4787` (12 assertions, four
  testsets) covers `bswap(UInt8/16/32/64)` (Int8/16/32 too),
  Int64 regression guard, and type preservation
  (`typeof(bswap(UInt16(...)))` === `UInt16`).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Bit ops respect element bit width for non-Int64 integer types ✅ (Issue #4785)

- `count_zeros`, `leading_zeros`, `leading_ones` (and `bitreverse`)
  for non-Int64 integer types returned wrong results because the
  compile path coerced the argument to I64 via
  `compile_expr_as(..., ValueType::I64)`. The runtime arm then
  operated on a 64-bit value, inflating zero counts due to
  implicit zero-extension. Example:
  `count_zeros(UInt8(0xf0))` returned 60 (should be 4) — the upper
  56 zero bits of the zero-extended Int64 leaked into the count.
- `count_ones`, `trailing_zeros`, `trailing_ones` already worked
  coincidentally because they count from the LSB and the
  upper-zero-extension doesn't affect them — but they shared the
  same root cause and would have misbehaved on signed-negative
  inputs (sign extension fills upper bits with ones).
- Fix:
  - `subset_julia_vm_compile/src/compile/expr/builtin_math.rs` — bit-op
    arms no longer pre-coerce via `compile_expr_as(...)`. They
    use plain `compile_expr` so the runtime sees the original
    integer variant.
  - `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/builtins_math.rs` — all 7 bit-op
    runtime arms (`CountOnes`, `CountZeros`, `LeadingZeros`,
    `LeadingOnes`, `TrailingZeros`, `TrailingOnes`, `Bitreverse`)
    pop a `Value` and match-dispatch over every integer variant
    (I8/I16/I32/I64/I128, U8/U16/U32/U64/U128, plus Bool for
    count_ones/zeros).
  - `bitreverse` now preserves the element type (UInt8 →
    UInt8, was previously coerced to Int64).
- New fixture `numeric_bit_ops_width_4785` (24 assertions, five
  testsets) covers count_zeros/leading_zeros/leading_ones for
  UInt8/16/32, Int8, signed-Int64 regression guards, and the
  bitreverse type-preservation case.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green;
  parity probe still reports 3 known divergences (all #4779), no
  new ones introduced.

### Symbol(parts...) multi-arg constructor ✅ (Issue #4780)

- `Symbol(parts...)` with multiple arguments failed at compile
  time with `Compilation error: Symbol requires exactly 1
  argument: Symbol(name)`. Upstream Julia's
  `Base.Symbol(args...) = Symbol(string(args...))` concatenates
  all parts via `string` then forms a single Symbol — common
  idiom for programmatically-built symbols like
  `Symbol("col_", i)` to build per-column accessor symbols.
- Fix:
  - `subset_julia_vm_compile/src/compile/expr/builtin.rs` —
    `BuiltinOp::SymbolNew` arm accepts `args.len() >= 1` and
    emits the full argc.
  - `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/builtins_macro/mod.rs` —
    `BuiltinId::SymbolNew` arm pops `argc` values, formats each
    via `format_value_print`, concatenates, and forms the
    Symbol. The 1-arg fast path stays in `vm/exec/call.rs`.
- New fixture `meta_symbol_multi_arg_4780` (7 assertions, five
  testsets) covers single-arg (regression guard), `Symbol("col_", 1)`
  / `Symbol("my", "_", "var")` / `Symbol(:prefix, "_", :suffix)`
  / five-part `Symbol("a", "b", "c", "d", "e")`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### NamedTuple / Tuple field show form (and single-element trailing comma) ✅ (Issue #4777)

- `string(::NamedTuple)` / `string(::Tuple)` / `print(buf, ::Tuple)`

  String/Char values lost their quotes — `(x = 1, y = hi, z = c)`
  vs upstream `(x = 1, y = "hi", z = 'c')`. Sibling of the
  already-fixed #4764 (struct field show form) — same root cause
  family but for the NamedTuple- and Tuple-specific format arms
  in `format_value_slow`.
- Also: single-element Tuple format produced `(1)` instead of the
  upstream-required `(1,)` disambiguation form.
- Fix: NamedTuple and Tuple value mapping in
  `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` now uses
  `format_value_show_field` (which quotes `Value::Str` and
  `Value::Char`), and the Tuple arm adds the trailing-comma case
  for single-element tuples.
- New fixture `io_namedtuple_tuple_show_form_4777` (8 assertions,
  five testsets) asserts:
  - NamedTuple/Tuple string/print quoting for String + Char
  - Single-element Tuple `(1,)` / `("hi",)` trailing comma
  - Empty Tuple `()` (no spurious comma)
  - Pure-numeric Tuple `(1, 2, 3)` unchanged
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Matrix fixture for Container<user_struct> StructRef leak + Dict/Set fixes ✅ (Issue #4774)

- Prevention sibling for the fix family #4761 / #4763 / #4772 /
  #4773. Existing matrix fixtures (#4757, #4766) covered (entry
  point) × (top-level value class) but did NOT cover
  (container shape × heap-allocated element). The PR #4771 /
  #4773 round-trip showed the gap is real.
- While writing the new matrix, two more leaks surfaced that the
  existing matrix didn't catch:
  - `Dict("k" => user_struct)` leaked `StructRef(heap_idx=N)`
    because `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` had no `Dict` arm.
  - `Set([1, 2, 3])` leaked `Set([I64(1), I64(2), I64(3)])`
    because the Set arm of `format_value_slow` used Rust
    `format!("{:?}", e)` for elements instead of the proper
    `format_dict_key` (which is what the Dict arm uses).
- Fix:
  - Add a `Value::Dict` recursion arm to
    `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` that rebuilds the Dict via
    `DictValue::with_type_params_opt` + per-entry `insert` so
    each value goes through the resolver.
  - Route `format_value_slow`'s Set arm through
    `format_dict_key` to eliminate the Rust Debug leak for set
    elements (parallels the Dict-key fix from #4735).
- New fixture `io_no_leak_container_struct_matrix_4774` (54
  assertions, 8 testsets) covers 7 container shapes (Vector,
  Tuple, NamedTuple, Dict<value=struct>, Pair<struct,Int>,
  Ref<struct>, Set<primitive>) × 6 display entry points
  (`string`, `repr`, `print(buf, x)`, multi-arg
  `print(buf, lit, x, lit)`, `sprint(io -> print(io, x))`,

  `Char(`, `Symbol(` tokens.
- Updated `docs/vm/CODE_AUDITS.md`'s "StructRef heap resolution"

### Vector{user_struct} StructRef leak inside compact form (regression) ✅ (Issue #4772)

- Regression from PR #4771 (#4770 fix). The new compact `[a, b, c]`
  form for `print(::Vector)` walked native-array elements via
  `format_value` without first resolving `Value::StructRef(idx)`
  against the struct heap, so a Vector of heap-allocated structs
  (any user struct, Pair, etc.) leaked `StructRef(heap_idx=N)`
  inside the compact form.
- Fix: extend `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` in
  `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` to recurse into both
  `Value::Memory` and `Value::NativeArray`, replacing the carrier
  with a fresh `Any`-typed copy whose elements are pre-resolved.
  The widening is throw-away (only used by the formatting copy of
  the value tree); original carriers are not mutated.
- New fixture `io_vector_struct_no_leak_4772` (20 assertions,
  three testsets) asserts that `string` / `repr` / `print(buf, x)`
  on Vector{user_struct}, Vector{Pair}, and Any-typed Vector with
  mixed struct elements no longer contain `StructRef` /
  `heap_idx=` tokens, and that the element values DO appear (so
  resolution actually fired rather than just hiding the leak).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### print(::Vector) / string(::Vector) compact form ✅ (Issue #4770)

- `print(v)` / `println(v)` / `string(v)` for any `Vector{T}` /
  `Matrix{T}` (e.g. from `[1, 2, 3]`, `sort([3, 1, 2])`,
  `filter(iseven, 1:6)`) leaked the internal Pure-Julia Array
  wrapper struct form:
  `Array{Int64}(3-element Memory{Int64}:\n 2\n 4\n 6, (3))` —
  exposing the `Memory{T}` carrier and shape tuple instead of the
  canonical `[2, 4, 6]`. Sibling of the already-fixed #4731 (which
  fixed `repr(::Vector)`); same family but for the print path.
- Fix: add an Array-wrapper arm to `format_struct_instance` in
  `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` that walks the `_mem`
  Memory carrier and emits the compact `[a, b, c]` (1D) /
  `[a b; c d]` (2D, column-major) / `T[]` (empty 0/1D) /
  `Matrix{T}(undef, r, c)` (empty 2D) form. Elements render
  through `format_value_show_field`, so String elements are
  quoted (matching upstream and #4764). Mirrors the Pure-Julia
  `_show_vector_compact` / `_show_matrix_compact` helpers.
- New fixture `io_print_vector_compact_4770` (9 assertions, five
  testsets) asserts `string` / `print(buf, ...)` produce the
  compact form for `Vector{Int}`, `Vector{String}`, typed empty
  vectors, matrices, and sort/filter results.
- This closes the easy slice of #4770 (1D/2D arrays). Higher-rank
  arrays (`ndims >= 3`) still fall through to the generic
  struct-field-dump arm; that case is uncommon for `print` usage
  and is left for follow-up.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Generic show(io, x) fallback for user-defined structs ✅ (Issue #4768)

- `repr(user_struct_instance)` crashed with "indexing not supported
  for I64(N)" for any user-defined struct. The Pure-Julia
  `repr` impl calls `show(io, x)`, but there was no fallback

  (Bool, Int*, Float*, String, Symbol, Tuple, Pair, Dict, ...)
  had explicit show methods. Dispatch silently fell through to a

  (Dict/Set/Missing/StepRangeLen show crashes that landed on

  `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/io.jl` that prints
  `typeof(x)(field1, field2, ...)` using `fieldnames(typeof(x))`
  + `getfield(x, name)` + recursive `show` per field. Specific
  arms for built-in types still win via most-specific-method
  dispatch.
- New fixture `io_show_fallback_user_struct_4768` (13 assertions,
  three testsets) asserts `repr` works for 1/2/3-field structs,
  built-in specific arms still produce the expected forms
  (Pair/Tuple/Array/String/Symbol/Float/Bool/Nothing/Missing),
  and `show(buf, ::user_struct)` writes the expected form into
  an IOBuffer.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Matrix-fixture and audit policy for StructRef leak prevention at IOBuffer entry points ✅ (Issue #4766)

- Prevention for the fix family #4761 / #4763. The original matrix

- Added "**StructRef heap resolution at every display entry

  Value-to-string and Rust Debug catch-all bullets, with the

### struct field formatting uses show form (quoted strings/chars) ✅ (Issue #4764)

- `print(io, struct)` / `string(struct)` recursed into fields using
  the print form (bare) instead of the show form, so String / Char
  fields lost their quotes (`Foo(42, hi)` vs upstream
  `Foo(42, "hi")`). Surfaced after #4761 made the StructRef leak
  visible.
- Fix: added `format_value_show_field` in
  `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/formatting.rs` that quotes `Value::Str`
  with `"..."` (escape table mirrors `escape_for_repr_str` in
  `builtins_strings.rs`), single-quotes `Value::Char` with
  `'...'`, and falls through to `format_value` for all other
  variants. `format_struct_instance` now maps fields through this
  helper for both the generic struct arm and the special-cased
  `Pair` arm.
- New fixture `io_struct_field_show_form_4764` (6 assertions, five
  testsets) asserts `string` / `print(buf, ...)` produce the
  quoted-field form for String / Char field types and that
  numeric fields are unchanged.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### print(io, struct) Rust Debug leak (StructRef heap_idx) ✅ (Issue #4761)

- `print(buf::IOBuffer, x)`, `print(stdout, x)` (the multi-arg
  IOPrint path), and `write(buf, x)` leaked the Rust debug repr
  `StructRef(heap_idx=N)` whenever `x` was a heap-allocated struct
  (`Pair(1, 2)`, user struct, etc.). The single-arg `print(x)` arm
  (`BuiltinId::Print`) already resolved StructRef via
  `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` before formatting, but the
  multi-arg IOPrint and IOWrite arms did not.
- Fix: resolve every `Value::StructRef` in the printed args against
  `self.struct_heap` before calling `format_value_print` in
  `subset_julia_vm_vm/src/vm/builtins_io.rs`'s `BuiltinId::IOPrint`
  (sprint / stdout / stderr / IOBuffer / non-IO arms) and
  `BuiltinId::IOWrite`. Mirrors the existing `BuiltinId::Print`
  pattern.
- New fixture `io_print_iobuffer_structref_4761` (8 assertions,
  three testsets) asserts `print(buf, Pair(...))`,
  `print(buf, user_struct)`, and multi-arg `print(buf, ..., x, ...)`
  no longer contain `StructRef` / `heap_idx` tokens and match the
  expected Julia form.
- This is the "easy slice" of #4761. The harder slice (route
  `print(buf, ...)` and `string(...)` through user-defined Pure
  Julia `show(io, ::T)` method lookup so e.g.
  `print(buf, LinRange(...))` calls the user's show method instead
  of dumping the 4 internal struct fields) remains open on #4761.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### show/repr for StepRangeLen with float step and LinRange ✅ (Issue #4759)

- `repr(1:0.5:3)` (and `show(io, ::StepRangeLen{Float64})` more
  generally) crashed with `GetField(0): expected struct, got Range
  in show(IO, CartesianIndex)` because the Pure-Julia
  `first/last/step(::StepRangeLen)` methods access struct fields,
  but VM-native `Value::Range` is reported as `StepRangeLen` yet is
  not backed by struct fields. Same crash family as the recent
  Dict/Set/Missing show fixes (#4737/#4739/#4743) but for ranges.
- Fix: add `show(io, ::StepRangeLen)` and `show(io, ::LinRange)`
  in `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/io.jl`, forwarding to an
  untyped helper (`_show_steprangelen_dynamic(io, r)`) that lacks
  the `::StepRangeLen` parameter annotation — this forces
  `first/last/step(r)` inside the helper to be dynamically
  dispatched, which routes through the VM Range builtins for
  VM-native ranges while still working for real struct values.
- New fixture `io_show_steprangelen_4759` (9 assertions, three
  testsets) covers `repr` / `show` / `string` for VM-native
  `StepRangeLen{Float64}` ranges and `repr` / `show` for
  `LinRange`. Tests use non-whole-number floats to avoid #4760
  (whole-number Float64 ranges narrow to Int64) and exclude
  `print(buf, ::LinRange)` / `string(::LinRange)` to avoid #4761
  (struct print/string bypass show methods).
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings, audits green.

### Rust Debug catch-all leak matrix fixture ✅ (Issue #4757)

### Stop ExprValue Display from leaking Rust Debug for non-I64/F64 children ✅ (Issue #4755)

- `Meta.parse("-9223372036854775808")` (working after PR #4754
  / Issue #4753) displayed as `Expr(:call, :-, I128(9223372036854775808))`
  — leaking the Rust `Debug` repr `I128(...)` into user output.
- `vm/value/container.rs`'s `impl Display for ExprValue`'s child
  arg match had explicit arms only for `I64` / `F64` / `Symbol` /
  `Str` / `Expr`; everything else fell into `_ => write!("{:?}")`.
  Extended with explicit arms for `I8`/`I16`/`I32`/`I128`,
  `U8`/`U16`/`U32`/`U64`/`U128`, `Bool`, `F16`/`F32`, `Char`,
  `Nothing`, `Missing`. The catch-all Debug fallback remains for
  values that have no parseable Julia literal form.
- New fixture `io_expr_display_no_debug_leak_4755` (6 assertions)
  asserts that `string(Meta.parse(...))` output never contains
  Rust Debug tokens like `I128(`, `Str(`, `Char(`. The fixture is
  runtime-agnostic — upstream Julia's `:(...)` form also never
  contains those tokens — so it passes under both interpreters.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining: sjulia's Expr display still uses the
  `Expr(:call, :+, :x, 1)` constructor form rather than upstream's
  `:(x + 1)` infix-quote form. Broader display-form parity is a
  separate follow-up.

### Meta.parse promotes overflowing integer literals to Int128/BigInt ✅ (Issue #4753)

- `Meta.parse("-9223372036854775808")` (i.e. `repr(typemin(Int64))`)
  failed at runtime with `Invalid integer: 9223372036854775808`.
  sjulia parsed the magnitude as a positive i64 *before* applying
  the unary `-`, and `Int64::MAX + 1` doesn't fit i64.
- Two-part fix:
  1. `vm/builtins_macro/parse.rs` `IntegerLiteral` arm falls
     back i64 → i128 → BigInt (for decimal literals only — hex /
     oct / bin keep the existing i64 path). The magnitude
     `9223372036854775808` now parses as `Value::I128`.
  2. `vm/builtins_macro/eval.rs` `eval_call` unary `-` arm handles
     `Value::I128` (and `Value::F32` while we're there). When the
     negation result fits `i64::try_from`, narrow back to
     `Value::I64` so the typing matches upstream
     (`typeof(-Int128(9223372036854775808)) === Int64`).
- New fixture `io_meta_parse_typemin_4753` (9 assertions) covers
  `typemin(Int64)` round-trip, overflow promotion to Int128/BigInt,
  and regular small negative literals (regression guard). All pass
  under both sjulia and upstream Julia 1.12 via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining out-of-scope cosmetic: the `Expr` display still leaks
  `I128(...)` Rust Debug repr (`Expr(:call, :-, I128(...))` instead
  of `:(-9223372036854775808)`); separate display-leak family
  tracked elsewhere.

### repr output matrix regression guard ✅ (Issue #4751)

- The session shipped 13 repr/show fixes in two days (#4725 through
  #4749) and the prevention issue called for a single matrix
  fixture that pins all of them in one place.
- New fixture `io_repr_meta_parse_roundtrip_4751` (32 assertions,
  four testsets) asserts the exact `repr(x)` output for:
  - numeric primitives — `Int`, `Float64`, `-0.0` (PR #4746),
    `Float32` with `f0` suffix (PR #4748), `Float16` wrapper
  - escaped strings and chars (PR #4750)
  - `Symbol`, `Bool`, `Nothing`, `Missing` (PR #4744)
  - `Pair` (PR #4726), `Vector{Int}`/`Vector{Float64}`/`Vector{String}`,
    typed-empty `Int64[]` (PR #4734), `Tuple`
- Originally framed as a `eval(Meta.parse(repr(x))) ≡ x` round-trip
  invariant, but sjulia's `Meta.parse` / `eval` has its own gaps
  (`=>` not callable in eval context, `Float32` literal parser
  doesn't read `1.5f0`, `Inf` / `NaN` / `nothing` / `missing`
  not resolved as identifiers in eval scope). Switched to a
  literal-equality form that's strictly stronger for repr's actual
  contract and not blocked by those independent gaps.
- Verified 32/32 under both sjulia and upstream Julia 1.12 via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### repr / show for String and Char now escape special characters ✅ (Issue #4749)

- `repr("a\nb")` wrote a raw newline between `a` and `b` instead of
  the literal escape sequence `\n`, so the output failed to
  round-trip through `Meta.parse`. Same for `"\"\""`, `"\\"`, and
  `repr('\n')` / `repr('\\')` / `repr('\'')`.
- Two-layer fix:
  1. `vm/builtins_strings.rs` `BuiltinId::Repr` now wraps
     `Value::Str` and `Value::Char` arms with new
     `escape_for_repr_str` / `escape_for_repr_char` helpers that
     mirror upstream `Base.escape_string` (escapes `\\`, `"`,
     `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`, plus `'` for chars).
  2. Pure Julia `show(io::IO, x::String)` in `julia/base/io.jl`
     now delegates to `escape_string` (already defined in
     `base/strings/util.jl`). `show(io::IO, x::Char)` rewritten
     with an inline match on the same escape table.
- `print` and `string` paths keep the raw form
  (`string("a\nb") == "a\nb"`); only show / repr escape.
- New fixture `io_repr_string_char_escape_4749` (14 assertions)
  covers String/Char escaping plus the print/string parity. All
  pass under both sjulia and upstream Julia 1.12 via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

## 最新対応 (2026-05-27)

### repr(Float32) keeps f0 suffix, repr(Float16) keeps wrapper ✅ (Issue #4747)

- `repr(Float32(1.5))` returned `"1.5"` and `repr(Float16(1.5))`
  returned `"1.5"`, both dropping the typed-literal information so
  an `eval(Meta.parse(...))` round-trip landed at `Float64`.
- Updated `show(io::IO, x::Float32)` to `print(io, x, "f0")` and
  `show(io::IO, x::Float16)` to `print(io, "Float16(", x, ")")`
  in `julia/base/io.jl`. `print` and `string` still call
  `format_float32_julia` / `format_float16_julia` directly, so
  bare-form output (`"1.5"`) is preserved for the print path,
  matching upstream's print vs show distinction.
- New fixture `io_typed_float_repr_4747` (9 assertions) covers
  Float32/Float16 repr (suffix/wrapper) and Float64 (unchanged), plus
  the print/string bare-form parity. Parity-verified via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Preserve sign of -0.0 in float display ✅ (Issue #4745)

- `repr(-0.0)`, `string(-0.0)`, `"$(-0.0)"`, and `print(io, -0.0)`
  all returned `"0.0"` instead of upstream Julia's `"-0.0"`. Root
  cause: `format_float_julia`'s whole-number arm computes
  `format!("{}.0", x as i64)`, and `(-0.0_f64) as i64 == 0`, so the
  negative-zero sign was lost.
- Added a `is_sign_negative() && x == 0.0` guard to both
  `format_float_julia` (Float64) and `format_float32_julia`
  (Float32), mirroring the existing guard in
  `format_float16_julia`. The guard fires before the lossy i64
  cast and returns `"-0.0"` directly.
- New fixture `io_neg_zero_sign_4745` (11 assertions) covers
  `repr` / `string` / interpolation / `print` / `show` for `-0.0`
  plus a `signbit`/`iszero`/equality cross-check that the
  underlying IEEE 754 value semantics are unchanged. Parity-verified
  via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### show(io, ::Missing) added — repr(missing) no longer crashes ✅ (Issue #4743)

- `repr(missing)` crashed with the same `show(IO, CartesianIndex)`
  mis-dispatch family as Dict (#4737) and Set (#4739) because there
  was no Pure Julia `show(io, ::Missing)` method.
- Added `show(io::IO, ::Missing) = print(io, "missing")` to
  `julia/base/io.jl` next to the existing `show(io, ::Nothing)`.
  One-liner addition matching the convention.
- New fixture `io_repr_missing_4743` (6 assertions) covers
  repr/string/interpolation/show for Missing and a Nothing parity
  pair to make sure both stay aligned.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### Separate print vs show for Symbol — print writes bare name ✅ (Issue #4741)

- `print(io, :foo)` / `println(io, :foo)` / `"$(:foo)"` all wrote
  `:foo` (the show-form) instead of the bare `foo` upstream Julia
  produces. Root cause: `format_value` is shared between print and
  show codepaths and unconditionally produces `:foo` for Symbols.
- New helper `vm/formatting.rs::format_value_print(v)` strips the
  leading `:` for top-level `Value::Symbol` and delegates everything
  else to `format_value`. Symbols inside containers (e.g.
  `Dict(:k => 1)`) intentionally keep the `:` per upstream convention,
  so recursion stops at the top level.
- Routed every print-side call site through the new helper:
  - `vm/exec/print.rs` `Instr::PrintAny` / `PrintAnyNoNewline`
  - `vm/builtins_io.rs` `BuiltinId::Print` / `Println` / `IOPrint`
    (all five IOPrint dispatch arms — sprint_state / Stdout /
    Stderr / IOBuffer / non-IO fallback), and `IOWrite`
  - `vm/exec/string_ops.rs` `Instr::ToString` / `StringConcat`
- Because print is now bare for Symbol, `show(io::IO, x::Symbol)`
  in `julia/base/io.jl` could no longer rely on
  `print(io, x)` accidentally producing `:foo`. Switched its body
  to `print(io, ":", x)` so the show-form keeps the `:`.
- New fixture `io_print_symbol_bare_4741` (7 assertions) covers
  print/println/interpolation/string/show for Symbol. Parity-checked
  via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### show(io, ::AbstractSet) and NamedTuple bare-name display ✅ (Issue #4739 first slice)

- `repr(Set([1, 2, 3]))` crashed with the same `show(IO, CartesianIndex)`
  mis-dispatch family that Dict had (Issue #4737) — Set also lacked a
  Pure Julia `show(io, ::AbstractSet)` method, so the dispatcher's
  conservative AbstractUser match picked CartesianIndex's
  `getfield(x, 1)` body.
- `repr((x=1, y=2))` returned `(:x = 1, :y = 2)` instead of
  `(x = 1, y = 2)` because sjulia's `print(io, ::Symbol)` writes the
  show-form (with `:` prefix), and `show(io, ::NamedTuple)` looped
  `print(io, ks[i], ...)`.
- Fixes in `julia/base/io.jl`:
  - New `show(io::IO, s::AbstractSet)` emits `Set([e1, e2, ...])`
    via recursive `show(io, x)` for each element.
  - `show(io::IO, nt::NamedTuple)` switched to `print(io, string(ks[i]), ...)`
    so the field name comes out bare (matches upstream).
- New fixture `io_show_set_namedtuple_4739` (6 assertions) verifies
  Set 1-elem / String elem, NamedTuple 1- and 2-field, and the
  `string(nt) == repr(nt)` agreement. Parity-checked via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining out-of-scope: typed empty `Set{Int}()` → upstream
  `Set{Int64}()` vs sjulia `Set([])` (type-param prefix gap, same
  family as #4733).

### show(io, ::AbstractDict) added — repr(Dict) no longer crashes ✅ (Issue #4737)

- `repr(Dict("a" => 1, "b" => 2))` crashed with
  `Type error: GetField(0): expected struct, got Dict in show(IO, CartesianIndex)`.
  Pure Julia base lacked a `show(io, d::AbstractDict)` method, so
  the dispatcher's conservative AbstractUser match picked up
  `show(io, ::CartesianIndex)` and its body's
  `getfield(d, 1)` blew up on the Dict.
- `julia/base/io.jl` gains a `show(io::IO, d::AbstractDict)` that
  emits the same compact form `format_dict_value` already produces
  (PR #4736 / Issue #4735): `Dict("k" => v, ...)`. Each entry
  recursively dispatches `show(io, k)` and `show(io, v)`, so
  existing `show(io, ::String)` (quoted), `show(io, ::Symbol)`
  (`:` prefix), and numeric `show` methods all compose correctly.
- New fixture `io_repr_dict_no_crash_4737` (7 assertions) covers
  String / Symbol / Int keys, mixed value types, and the
  `repr(d) == string(d)` agreement assertion. Parity-verified via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining out-of-scope: upstream Julia's `Dict{T1,T2}` type-param
  prefix divergence is tracked separately.

### Dict String key/value Debug-leak in format_dict_value ✅ (Issue #4735)

- `string(Dict("a" => 1))` returned `"Dict(Str(\"a\") => 1)"`,
  leaking the Rust `Debug` repr of `DictKey::Str(...)` because
  `format_dict_value` formatted each key with `format!("{:?}", k)`.
  String *values* inside a Dict also rendered without quotes
  (`Dict(1 => "one")` → `"Dict(1 => one)"`) because `format_value`'s
  print contract drops the quote convention upstream uses inside
  container display.
- `vm/formatting.rs` `format_dict_value` is now factored into two
  helpers:
  1. `format_dict_key(k)` formats `DictKey` in Julia convention —
     `"<s>"` for `Str`, `:<s>` for `Symbol`, plain digits for signed
     ints, zero-padded `0x...` for `UInt*`, and the existing
     `format_float*_julia` helpers for `F16`/`F32`/`F64` bit-packed
     keys.
  2. `format_dict_value_field(v)` matches `Value::Str` to the
     quoted `"<s>"` form (show convention) while delegating
     everything else to `format_value` (print convention) — the
     scope of "switch to show inside containers" stays small.
- New fixture `io_dict_string_key_no_debug_leak_4735` (8 assertions)
  exercises String/Symbol/Int keys and String values. Parity-verified
  via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining out-of-scope: upstream Julia also includes a
  `Dict{T1,T2}` type-parameter prefix and converts `Bool` values to
  `1`/`0` inside Dict display. Tracked separately.

### Typed-empty-array repr preserves element type ✅ (Issue #4733)

- PR #4732 (Issue #4731) compactified `show(io, ::Array)` but left
  empty arrays rendering as plain `"[]"`. Upstream Julia preserves
  the element type in `repr(Int[])` → `"Int64[]"`,
  `repr(Float64[])` → `"Float64[]"`, etc. so the result can
  round-trip through `eval(Meta.parse(...))` back into the original
  typed vector instead of `Vector{Any}`.
- `julia/base/io.jl` `_show_vector_compact` and
  `_show_matrix_compact` gain `length(v) == 0` / `rows == 0 || cols == 0`
  special cases that emit `<eltype>[]` for vectors and
  `Matrix{<eltype>}(undef, rows, cols)` for matrices, matching the
  upstream constructor forms.
- New fixture `io_repr_typed_empty_array_4733` (10 assertions)
  covers `Int / Int64 / Float64 / Any / String / Bool` empty vectors
  plus the non-empty inline form from PR #4732. Parity-verified via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.

### repr([1,2,3]) IOBuffer leak + show(::Array) compact form ✅ (Issue #4731)

- `repr([1, 2, 3])` returned
  `"IOBuffer(...)\n3-element Vector{Int64}: 1\n 2\n 3\n"`. Two
  overlapping bugs:
  1. Pure Julia `_show_vector(io, v)` calls `println(io)` to add a
     trailing newline. `println(io::IO)` was dispatching through the
     stdout path (because the `io` parameter inferred as `Any`),
     formatting the IO value itself as `"IOBuffer(...)"` and dumping
     that to stdout.
  2. `show(io::IO, ::Array)` was writing the multi-line
     `MIME"text/plain"` form ("n-element Vector{T}: ...") instead of
     the compact 2-arg `show(io, x)` form ("[a, b, c]") that
     upstream Julia uses for `repr`.
- Fixes:
  1. `compile/expr/builtin_io.rs` extends the `println(...)` compile
     path: when the first arg is `ValueType::IO` *or*
     `ValueType::Any`, route through the `IOPrint` builtin which
     dispatches on the runtime kind. This catches the common case
     where an `io` parameter is untyped (`Any`) but actually holds
     an `IOBuffer` at runtime.
  2. `vm/builtins_io.rs` `BuiltinId::Println` gains an early
     `Value::IO` dispatch as a runtime safety net for any path that
     escapes the compile-time check.
  3. `julia/base/io.jl` adds `_show_vector_compact` and
     `_show_matrix_compact` helpers and switches
     `show(io::IO, ::Array)` to call them. The original
     `_show_vector` / `_show_matrix` are retained for the
     `MIME"text/plain"` REPL display form.
- New fixture `io_repr_array_compact_4731` (10 assertions) verifies
  `repr`, `string`, and `println(io)` parity. Parity-checked against
  upstream Julia 1.12 via `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 128/128 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings.
- Remaining: `repr(Int[])` returns `"[]"` in sjulia but `"Int64[]"`
  upstream. Tracked separately.

### String interpolation "$p" also stops leaking StructRef ✅ (Issue #4727)

### string(Pair) no longer leaks Rust `StructRef(heap_idx=N)` debug repr ✅ (Issue #4725)

- `string(Pair(1, 2))` returned `"StructRef(heap_idx=12)"`, and
  every code path that interpolated a heap-allocated `Pair` leaked
  the Rust `StructRef` `Debug` formatting into user output.
- Root cause: `vm/formatting.rs`'s `format_value` is heap-less, so
  `Value::StructRef` fell through to `format!("StructRef(heap_idx={})", idx)`.
- Added `vm/formatting.rs::resolve_struct_refs_for_format(v, heap)`
  which recursively walks composite carriers (`Tuple`, `NamedTuple`,
  `Ref`, `QuoteNode`, `Struct`) and replaces each `Value::StructRef`
  with its resolved `Value::Struct(StructInstance)`. The existing
  `format_struct_instance` gained a `Pair` arm (alongside the
  existing `Rational` arm) that renders `"left => right"` instead of
  the constructor-call form.
- `vm/builtins_strings.rs`'s `BuiltinId::StringNew` and
  `BuiltinId::Repr` now pass each argument through
  `resolve_struct_refs_for_format` before formatting, so
  `string(Pair(1,2))`, `repr(Pair(1,2))`, and `string((1, p))` all
  match upstream.
- New fixture `strings_string_pair_no_structref_leak_4725` (5 cases)
  exercises the fix under both interpreters via
  `scripts/fixture_julia_parity.sh`.
- 127/127 fixture tests pass, clippy 0 warnings. Out-of-scope sub-bugs
  (string interpolation `"$p"` and `string(Pair("a", 42))` show-vs-print
  for string fields) are tracked separately.

### string(x; base=N) accepts all integer widths and Bool ✅ (Issue #4723)

- `string(UInt8(255), base=16)`, `string(Int128(1) << 100, base=16)`,

  integer width failed at runtime with

  conversion`. `repr(0xff)` and similar typed-int formatting silently
  hit the same error because they routed through `string(...; base=N)`.

  (`I8/I16/I32/I64/I128`) and `F64` to `i128`, and unsigned widths
  (`U8/U16/U32/U64/U128`) plus `Bool` to `u128`. The format step is
  factored into a `format_unsigned` helper that handles bases

  iterative digit loop. Signed values prepend a `-` for negatives
  after formatting `unsigned_abs`; unsigned values format without a

  `string(n::Integer; base=10, pad=0)`.
- New fixture `strings_string_base_int_widths_4723` (21 cases)
  covers `Int{8,16,32,64,128}`, `UInt{8,16,32,64,128}`, and `Bool`

### Dispatcher no longer treats Array as matching AbstractString/AbstractDict ✅ (Issue #4708)

- After PR #4707 added per-type `summary` overloads, defining
  `f(::AbstractString)`, `f(::AbstractDict)`, and `f(::AbstractArray)`
  side by side triggered `AmbiguousMethod` for `f([1,2,3])` —
  the `JuliaType::AbstractUser` parent-`Any` fallback in
  `is_subtype_of` made `JuliaType::Array.is_subtype_of(Any)` return
  true and therefore claimed `Array <: AbstractDict` /
  `Array <: AbstractString` were both true.
- Fix in `types/julia_type/comparison.rs`'s `AbstractUser` arm:
  when the AbstractUser's declared parent is `Any`, skip the
  recursive parent fallback. Instead, defer to CoreType when the
  abstract name resolves to a builtin abstract
  (`CoreType::Abstract(_)`), so `Dict <: AbstractDict` and
  `Set <: AbstractSet` keep working. Non-`Any` parents (e.g.
  `AbstractArray`) retain the existing fallback so hierarchies
  like `AbstractVector <: AbstractArray` still resolve.
- The dispatcher's struct-ancestry tie-breaker in
  `compile/method_table.rs` continues to filter Struct args against
  the parent map, so existing Matrix/Vector dispatch tests
  (`matmul_matrix_matrix_abstract_dispatch_4020`,
  `nullspace_logdet_adjoint`) keep selecting the correct overload.
- New fixture `dispatch_abstract_dict_array_disambiguation_4708`
  (10 cases) reproduces the original bug and asserts the fix
  preserves Dict/Set/Array dispatch semantics. The same assertions
  pass under upstream Julia 1.12.

### INTENTIONAL_NOOP markers for essentials.jl no-op helpers ✅ (Issue #4703 first slice)

- First slice of the Pure Julia base/ silent-stub audit (Issue #4703).

### Base.isvarargtype / Base.isvatuple replace stub implementations ✅ (Issue #4701)

- `subset_julia_vm/src/julia/base/essentials.jl`'s `isvarargtype(t)`
  always returned `false` and `isvatuple(t)` returned `t === Tuple`,
  so `Base.isvarargtype(Vararg{Int})` and
  `Base.isvatuple(Tuple{Int, Vararg{Int}})` both returned wrong values.
- Replaced with upstream-equivalent Pure Julia implementations:
  `isvarargtype(t) = isa(t, DataType) && nameof(t) === :Vararg` and an
  `isvatuple` that unwraps UnionAlls then checks the last `.parameters`
  entry. This is now tractable thanks to `Base.unwrap_unionall`
  (PR #4693), the registry-backed `.parameters` projection (PR #4693 /
  PR #4695), and TypeVar preservation in parametric application
  (PR #4697).
- New fixture `reflection_isvarargtype_4701` (12 cases) exercises both
  helpers across `Vararg{Int}`, `Vararg{Float64}`, plain DataTypes, and
  tuple types with and without a trailing Vararg. The same assertions
  pass under upstream Julia 1.12.

### Const-positive refinement for sqrt/log DomainError inference ✅ (Issue #4274)

- Previously every call to `sqrt`, `log`, `log10`, `log2` reported
  `ExceptionType::Known("DomainError")` and `nothrow=false` regardless
  of the argument. Upstream Julia combines constprop with the same
  call:`Base.infer_exception_type(() -> sqrt(4))` returns `Union{}`
  (nothrow). `Base.infer_exception_type(() -> sqrt(-1))` stays
  `DomainError`.
- `typed_exception_type_for_expr` is now generalised beyond the
  numeric-division slice. When the single argument is a
  `LatticeType::Const(Int64(n))` with `n >= 0`, or
  `Const(Float64(f))` with non-NaN `f >= 0.0`, the call is refined to
  `nothrow=true` / `ExceptionType::Bottom`. Known-negative constants
  keep the conservative `DomainError` exception type but tighten
  effects to `effect_free_may_throw`.
- The pre-existing
  `test_issue_3714_inferred_expr_tracks_call_exception_effects`
  assumed `sqrt(1)` would throw DomainError. It is updated to cover
  const-negative (`sqrt(-1)` → DomainError), const-positive
  (`sqrt(4)` → Bottom), float const (`sqrt(2.5)` → Bottom), and the
  same const refinement for `log` / `log10` / `log2`.
- Verified against upstream: `() -> sqrt(4)` and `() -> log(2)` both
  yield `Union{}`; `sqrt(-1)` yields `DomainError`.
- Remaining gap: `log(-1)` is `Union{DomainError, InexactError}`
  upstream. Our `ExceptionType` cannot yet represent a union of
  exception types, so we conservatively return `DomainError` — left
  on the broader #4274 backlog.

### Runtime TypeVar preserved in Vector{T}/Dict{K,V}/struct{T} ✅ (Issue #4696)

- `T = TypeVar(:T)` followed by `Vector{T}` previously erased `T` to
  `Any`, so `Vector{T}.parameters[1]` returned `Any` instead of `T`.
  The `ConstructParametricType` instruction stringified its type
  arguments and dropped `Value::RuntimeTypeVar` into the generic
  `"Any"` fallback arm.
- `vm/exec/struct_ops.rs` now writes the TypeVar's name into the
  parametric string for the generic path and also accepts
  `Value::RuntimeTypeVar` via `tv.projection()` for the special-case
  `num_type_args == 1` constructors (`Vector` / `Matrix` / `Type`).
- The change unblocks the semantic round-trip with
  `UnionAll(var, body)` (Issue #4694): `UnionAll(S, Vector{S})` now
  produces a real `Vector{S} where S` instead of `Vector{Any} where S`,
  so `Base.rewrap_unionall` and friends compose correctly.
- New fixture `reflection_parametric_runtime_typevar_4696` (13 cases)
  asserts kind+name preservation for `Vector`, `Matrix`, `Dict`, and
  user-defined parametric structs. The same assertions pass under
  upstream Julia 1.12.
- Remaining gap: TypeVar **identity** (`===`) between the original
  fresh `RuntimeTypeVar` and the projected parameter is still not
  preserved. Tracked under the broader runtime type-object identity
  work in Issue #3909.

### UnionAll(var, body) constructor + Base.rewrap_unionall ✅ (Issue #4694)

- `UnionAll(TypeVar(:T), Vector{Int64})` previously failed with
  "Function 'UnionAll' not found", which blocked Pure Julia
  reflection helpers like `Base.rewrap_unionall` and
  `Base.rename_unionall`. This is the natural follow-up to PR #4693
  (Issue #3909) which added `Base.unwrap_unionall`.
- New `BuiltinId::UnionAll` registered in `builtins.rs`. The handler
  in `vm/builtins_types.rs` pops `(var, body)`, accepts both
  `Value::RuntimeTypeVar` and registry-projected
  `Value::DataType(JuliaType::TypeVar(...))` for `var`, and returns
  a fresh `JuliaType::UnionAll { var, bound, body }`.
- Matches upstream `jl_type_unionall`'s "smart wrap" semantics: when
  the body does not reference the bound variable, return the body
  unchanged. Two new helpers (`julia_type_references_typevar` and
  `parametric_struct_mentions_typevar`) walk the JuliaType structure
  and also scan string-encoded names like `"Vector{T}"` for the var
  via word-boundary matching. This keeps
  `UnionAll(T, Vector{Int64}) === Vector{Int64}` and
  `Base.rewrap_unionall(Int64, Vector) === Int64` in agreement with
  upstream Julia.
- `julia/base/essentials.jl` now defines
  `rewrap_unionall(t, u) = isa(u, UnionAll) ? UnionAll(u.var, rewrap_unionall(t, u.body)) : t`,
  closing the round-trip with `Base.unwrap_unionall`.
- New fixture `reflection_unionall_constructor_4694` (9 cases)
  exercises the smart wrap and round-trip. The same assertions also
  pass under upstream Julia 1.12.

### isa kind agrees with typeof for runtime type objects + Base.unwrap_unionall ✅ (Issue #3909)

- `typeof(Vector) === UnionAll` was returning true but `isa(Vector, UnionAll)`
  returned false (and `isa(Vector, DataType)` returned true) because
  `Value::DataType(_)` always projected to `JuliaType::DataType` through
  `runtime_type()`, bypassing the kind classification owned by
  `RuntimeTypeRegistry`.
- `vm/builtins_types.rs`'s `BuiltinId::Isa` now routes `Value::DataType(jt)`
  through `RuntimeTypeRegistry::new_with_struct_defs(...).object(jt)
  .runtime_type_projection()`, which yields the registry's kind projection
  (`JuliaType::DataType`, `Struct("UnionAll")`, `Struct("TypeVar")`).
- `types/julia_type/comparison.rs`'s `JuliaType::Type` arm now also accepts
  `Struct("UnionAll")` so `isa(Vector, Type)` keeps returning true.
- `vm/exec/struct_ops.rs`'s `Instr::GetFieldByName` gained a
  `Value::DataType(jt)` block mirroring the static `ValueType::DataType`
  path in `compile/expr/struct_.rs`. Pure Julia helpers can now access
  `.parameters`, `.var`, `.body`, `.name`, `.lb`, `.ub` on a type-object
  value even when inference could not narrow the carrier to
  `ValueType::DataType` (e.g. parameters typed `Any`).
- `julia/base/essentials.jl`'s `unwrap_unionall(t)` was a stub returning
  `t` unchanged. Reimplemented as
  `while isa(t, UnionAll); t = t.body; end; return t`, matching upstream
  Julia's `Base.unwrap_unionall`.
- New fixture `reflection_isa_typeof_kind_consistency_3909` (24 cases)
  covers isa kind agreement and `Base.unwrap_unionall`. Verified the same
  assertions pass under upstream Julia.

### specializer widens slot type on incompatible reassignment ✅ (Issue #4688)

- `FunctionSpecializer::Stmt::Assign` previously overwrote
  `self.locals[var]` with each assignment's concrete type. For patterns
  like `x = "init"; for i in 1:n; x = 42; end; x` the body's `x = 42`
  latched `locals[x] = I64`, so the final read of `x` compiled to
  `LoadI64` (slot-rewritten to `LoadSlotI64`). When the loop ran zero
  iterations the slot still held the surviving `Str("init")` from the
  pre-loop store, and `LoadSlotI64` crashed with
  `expected numeric in x, got Str("init")`.
- `Stmt::Assign` now widens the *recorded* slot type to `ValueType::Any`
  whenever the previous binding had a different concrete type. The
  store itself still uses the value's concrete type (`StoreI64`,
  `StoreStr`, etc.) because the runtime slot is `Option<Value>` and can
  hold any tag. The widening only affects later `LoadXxx` emissions,
  which become `LoadAny` / `LoadSlot` (untyped) and read whichever
  concrete tag survived to that program point.
- The generic compiler (`compile/stmt.rs`'s `Stmt::Assign`) already
  handled the same case via `mixed_type_vars` populated by inference
  (Issues #3535 / #3536). This change brings the specializer to parity
  without copying the full mixed-type-vars infrastructure: the
  one-step type-changed guard is enough because the specializer
  visits each assignment in source order.
- Added `type_inference_slot_widening_4688` (10 cases) covering
  int/str/float overwrite inside a parametric for-loop and a partial
  `if` rebind. All match upstream Julia.

### specializer patches break/continue in for/while/foreach ✅ (Issue #4684)

- `FunctionSpecializer` (`vm/specialize/stmt.rs`)'s `compile_for`,
  `compile_while`, and `compile_foreach` never patched the placeholder
  `Jump(0)` instructions emitted by `Stmt::Break` and `Stmt::Continue`
  inside the loop body. After the call site relocated specialized
  bytecode by `entry_point` (`vm/exec/call.rs`), each unpatched
  `Jump(0)` became `Jump(entry_point)` — an unconditional jump back to
  the start of the specialized function — and any parametric-range
  for-loop with a top-level `break` would loop forever (the original
  Issue #4684 reproduction never returned).
- Each loop compiler now saves the enclosing loop's pending
  `break_positions` / `continue_positions` via `std::mem::take`,
  compiles the body, patches every entry the body accumulated to the
  correct target (loop exit for break, `continue_target` for `for` /
  `foreach`, `loop_start` for `while`), and restores the outer loop's
  pending lists so nested loops route their own break/continue
  correctly.
- Added `control_flow_for_break_dynamic_range_4684` covering
  top-level break, break with assignment, break with String overwrite,
  `continue`, conditional break inside an `if`, and a nested-loop
  inner-break — 15 assertions matching upstream Julia. Issue #4680's
  fixture (`type_inference_for_break_const_range_4680.jl`) intentionally
  omitted the dynamic `1:n` runtime call because of this hang; that
  case is now safe to exercise on sjulia (left as a future follow-up
  PR alongside the fixture extension).

### call-site `==` against Union-typed function return defers to runtime dispatch ✅ (Issue #4686)

- Root cause of Issue #4682 (closed by PR #4685's regression fixture
  after the constant-range narrowing in PR #4683 sidestepped it). The
  `Str-vs-non-Str` shortcut in `compile/expr/binary/mod.rs`
  constant-folded `==` to `false` whenever exactly one side had
  `ValueType::Str` and the other was neither `Str` nor `Any`. The
  shortcut did not account for `ValueType::Union(_)`: a slot inferred
  as `Union{Int64, String}` can hold a `String` at runtime that should
  compare equal to the literal on the other side, but the compiler
  emitted `PushBool(false)` and silently miscompiled `f() == "s"`.
- Extended `left_is_runtime_unknown` / `right_is_runtime_unknown` to
  match `ValueType::Any | ValueType::Union(_)` so Union-typed operands
  fall through to the runtime-dispatch path already shared with `Any`
  (`has_any` at the end of the function). For Unions that don't
  include `Str` (e.g. `Union{Int64, Float64} == "s"`) the runtime path
  still returns `false`, just via dispatch instead of constant folding
  — correctness is preserved, the only cost is a slightly later
  decision point.
- Added `comparison_union_eq_string_4686` exercising the
  Union-returning for-loop call site, the reverse polarity (`"s" ==
  f()`), the via-binding path, the Int-arm runtime value, and an
  if-Union end-to-end flow. Skipped the `Union{Int64, String}` slot
  with a String runtime value in the loop-zero-iteration case because
  it trips a separate `LoadSlotI64` slot-allocator bug not in scope
  for this PR.

### for-loop + break over non-empty constant range narrows post-loop env ✅ (Issue #4680)

- Follow-up to PR #4678 / PR #4681 (Issues #4267, #4679). Upstream Julia
  models `for var in start:end` over a provably-non-empty constant
  range with a top-level `break` as exiting only via the break edge —
  the pre-loop env never falls through because the loop is guaranteed
  to run at least once, and the end-of-iteration env is unreachable
  past the break. sjulia previously merged the pre-loop env into the
  post-loop env, producing wider `Union{...}` returns (e.g. the issue's
  `for i in 1:3; x = "s"; break; end` returning `Union{Int64, String}`
  instead of `String`).
- Added `InferenceEngine::range_provably_non_empty`, a constant-bounds
  oracle over the `start`/`end`/optional `step` lattice values. It
  recognizes `Const(Int64)` triples and applies the sign-of-step rule
  (`step > 0 ⇒ start ≤ end`, `step < 0 ⇒ start ≥ end`, `step = 0 ⇒
  empty`), and bails out for dynamic bounds, non-integer types, and
  other unknown shapes. Float ranges are intentionally left out of this
  slice because of their rounding edge cases.
- `Stmt::For` now computes `range_non_empty` up front and inspects the
  body for a top-level `Stmt::Break` (`body_has_direct_break`). When
  both hold the post-loop env is replaced with the joined break-exit
  env — mirroring the statically-true `while` slice. When the break is
  nested in an `if`/`try` the end-of-range exit edge is still
  reachable, so the legacy pre-loop merge is preserved. This matches
  upstream Julia's behavior of keeping the `Union{...}` for the
  conditional-break case.
- Added `type_inference_for_break_const_range_4680` exercising the
  basic `1:3` repro, `1:2:6`/`5:-1:1` step variants, a pre-existing
  `String` overwrite, a nested-break case, and a dynamic `1:n` contrast
  that should keep the wider `Union{Int64, String}` to lock in the
  precision difference. Both runtime (`===`) and `Base.return_types` /
  `Base.infer_return_type` are checked. The existing
  `type_inference_while_true_break_4267` and
  `type_inference_for_range_loop_var_type` fixtures continue to pass,
  per the issue's acceptance criteria.
- Discovered while implementing this slice (both surface separately,
  not blocked on #4680):
  - `for_v() == "s"` at the call site returns `false` even though
    `typeof(for_v()) === String` and `for_v() === "s"` is `true` —
    likely a codegen path for static dispatch of `==` after a
    for-loop. Filed as Issue #4682.
  - `for i in 1:n; ...; break; end` (parametric range, top-level
    break) hangs sjulia at runtime even though inference returns the
    correct `Union{Int64, String}`. The fixture uses constant ranges
    for runtime checks and only asserts inference for the dynamic
    `1:n` case to avoid this hang.

### `while true` no-exit collapses post-loop env to `Union{}` ✅ (Issue #4679)

- Follow-up to PR #4678 (Issue #4267 break-env slice). Upstream Julia
  models a statically-true `while` whose body has no `break`,
  `return`, or `throw` as never falling through and surfaces the
  post-loop env as `Union{}` (Bottom), so the enclosing function
  return type collapses to `Union{}`. sjulia previously kept the body
  fixpoint output, producing a sound-but-wider `Int64`/etc.
- Added a `StmtResult::Diverges` variant. `Stmt::While` now emits it
  when `condition_always_true` is true, the break-env stack slot is
  empty, and no explicit `return` was accumulated. `infer_block_branch`
  treats this as a non-falling statement: it drops `last_stmt_type` to
  `LatticeType::Bottom`, sets `may_fallthrough = false`, and stops
  iterating since subsequent statements are unreachable in the
  abstract domain. `infer_block_explicit_return_only` and
  `infer_block_partial_struct_return` route `Diverges` the same way.
- `lattice_to_parametric_julia_type` now preserves
  `LatticeType::Bottom` as `JuliaType::Bottom`. The legacy
  `LatticeType::Bottom → ValueType::Any` fallback in
  `lattice_to_value_type` would otherwise widen `Union{}` back to
  `Any` when reflection's `m.return_type` snapshot is materialized
  via `value_type_to_julia_type`.
- Added `type_inference_while_true_no_exit_4679` exercising the basic
  no-break loop, dead-code-after-loop, `Const(true)` variable
  condition, nested outer-no-break/inner-break, and pure literal
  `while true` cases — runtime, `Base.return_types`, and
  `Base.infer_return_type` all match upstream Julia returning
  `Union{}`. Existing `type_inference_while_true_break_4267` and
  `type_inference_while_exit_narrowing_4267` continue to pass.
- Base call sites in `base/dict.jl` and `base/reflection.jl` use
  `while true` with `return` exits inside the body, so
  `accumulated_return` is `Some(_)` and the new `Diverges` branch is
  not taken there — `MaybeReturn` semantics preserved.

### statically-true while + break exit narrowing ✅ (Issue #4267)

- Added a per-loop break-env stack on `InferenceEngine`. `Stmt::Break` now
  snapshots the current path-sensitive env into the innermost loop's slot;
  `while`/`for`/`foreach` push and pop the slot so nested loops dispatch
  breaks to the correct target.
- `Stmt::While` detects statically-true conditions (literal `Bool(true)`
  or a variable bound to `Const(true)`). For those loops the post-loop
  env is the joined break-exit env when at least one break was seen, since
  the condition-false exit edge is unreachable.
- When the always-true loop has no break, the body fixpoint output is
  retained as a sound over-approximation of the infinite-loop case
  (upstream Julia marks this as `Union{}`; sjulia still keeps that as
  follow-up work).
- Existing `Stmt::While` handling for non-statically-true conditions is
  unchanged — pre-loop merge and exit narrowing still apply, so the
  Issue #3517 / #4267 first-slice cases continue to pass.
- Added `type_inference_while_true_break_4267`, covering single break,
  const-true condition, break-in-if, overwriting break, and nested
  while-true via runtime, `Base.infer_return_type`, and `Base.return_types`
  parity against upstream Julia.
- Keeping #4267 open for the broader goal: routing production inference
  through lowered CFG blocks, block input/output state, statement side
  tables, and Phi/SSA value typing.
